# Configure PagerDuty as a data pipeline source

Set up PagerDuty as a data pipeline source to extract incident, on-call, and incident analytics data from the PagerDuty REST API and sync it to your destination.

Use this guide to review the prerequisites, generate a PagerDuty API key, connect PagerDuty as a data pipeline source, configure the pipeline, and understand the supported objects, sync modes, schema and data type handling, sensitive data handling, and limitations.

## PagerDuty features supported

The following features are supported when you use PagerDuty as a pipeline source:

- **Cloud connectivity**: Connect to PagerDuty over HTTPS through `https://api.pagerduty.com`. On-prem agents aren't required.
- **Object-level selection**: Choose which PagerDuty objects to sync to your destination.
- **Full sync, incremental sync, and append-only sync**: Supports full sync, incremental sync, and append-only sync, configured for each object. Refer to [Sync modes](#sync-modes) for more information.
- **Schema drift detection and handling**: Detect and apply schema changes automatically with **Auto-sync new fields**, or keep the schema fixed with **Block new fields**.
- **Field-level data protection**: Hash or replicate sensitive fields as is before the data reaches your destination.
- **Configurable sync frequency**: Schedule syncs on a time-based interval or with a cron expression. The minimum supported interval is 15 minutes.

## PagerDuty prerequisites

Connecting PagerDuty as a data pipeline source requires:

- A PagerDuty account
- Credentials for your chosen authentication method:
  - **API key**: A read-only PagerDuty General access API key. Refer to [Generate a PagerDuty API key](#generate-a-pagerduty-api-key) for setup steps.
- Optional. A Business or higher PagerDuty plan to sync `Audit Records`, `Analytics Raw Incidents`, and `Analytics Metrics Incidents`. PagerDuty offers `Incident Workflows` on Business and Enterprise plans, with limited availability on Professional plans. Refer to [Limitations](#limitations) for more information.

> **REQUIRED PERMISSIONS**
> 
> Workato recommends a General access API key scoped to read-only access for data extraction only. This is the same key type PagerDuty's existing Workato connector for recipes and automations uses, but that connector requires read and write permissions. Don't reuse a read/write key for your data pipeline connection.

## Generate a PagerDuty API key

Complete the following steps to generate a read-only PagerDuty General access API key in your PagerDuty account:

1. Go to **Integrations > Developer Tools > API Access Keys** in your PagerDuty account and click **Create New API Key**.
   
2. Enter a description that identifies the key, such as `Workato data pipeline`.
   
3. Select the **Read-only API key** checkbox.
   
4. Copy the generated API key and store it in a secure location. You need this value to create the Workato connection.
   

> **USE A READ-ONLY KEY**
> 
> A read/write API key grants your data pipeline connection more access than it needs. Select the **Read-only API key** checkbox when you generate the key to limit the connection to read access only.

### Permissions

You must have an Admin, Global Admin, or Account Owner role in PagerDuty to create an API key. Contact an Admin or Account Owner in your organization to create this key if you don't have one of these roles.

## Supported connection types

PagerDuty data pipelines support one authentication method:

- **API key**: Provide a read-only General access API key generated from your PagerDuty account. Refer to [Generate a PagerDuty API key](#generate-a-pagerduty-api-key) for setup steps.

Personal API keys aren't supported, because they're scoped to individual user permissions and can't guarantee account-wide read access. OAuth 2.0 isn't currently supported for PagerDuty data pipelines.

## Connect to PagerDuty

Connect to PagerDuty

Complete the following steps to connect to PagerDuty in Workato:

1. Select **Create > Connection** or press C twice.
   
2. Search for `PagerDuty` and select it as your app.
   
3. Enter a name in the **Connection name** field.
   
4. Use the **Location** drop-down menu to select the project where you plan to store the connection.
   
5. Use the **Region** drop-down menu to select **US** or **EU**, matching your PagerDuty account's hosting region. Defaults to **US**. You can't change this value after you create the connection.
   
6. Enter the API key you generated in the **API key** field.
   
7. Select **Connect** to verify and save the connection. Workato displays a success message when the connection is established.
   

## Configure the pipeline

Complete the following steps to configure PagerDuty as your data pipeline source:

1. Select **Create > Data pipeline**.
   
2. Enter a name for the data pipeline in the **Data pipeline name** field.
   
   ![Data pipeline setup](/assets/set-up-pipeline.Cxx6hIk2.png)_Data pipeline setup_
   
3. Use the **Location** drop-down menu to select the project where you plan to store the data pipeline.
   
4. Click **Start building**.
   
5. Click the **Extract new/updated records from source app** trigger. This trigger defines how the pipeline retrieves data from PagerDuty.
   
   ![Configure the Extract new/updated records from source app trigger](/assets/choose-source-app.B2OOUpgY.png)_Configure the Extract new/updated records from source app trigger_
   
6. Use the **Your Connected Source Apps** drop-down menu to select **PagerDuty**.
   
7. Choose the PagerDuty connection you plan to use for this pipeline. Alternatively, click **\+ New connection** to create a new connection.
   
8. Click **Add object** to open the **Add new objects** panel.
   
   ![Add objects](/assets/add-objects-pagerduty.CAJcy0sO.png)_Add objects_
   
9. Search or browse the list of available PagerDuty objects, select the objects you plan to sync, and click **Add**.
   
10. Review and customize the schema for each selected object. The pipeline automatically fetches an object's schema when you select it, so the destination matches the source.
    
    Expand an object to view associated fields. Keep all fields selected to extract all available data, or deselect specific fields to exclude them from data extraction and schema replication.
    
11. Optional. Configure the sync mode for an object:
    
    1. Click the **Settings** (gear) icon next to the object.
       
    2. Select a **Sync mode**:
       
       - **Incremental**: Sync only new records.
       - **Full sync**: Reload all records on each run.
       
       Workato defaults to **Full sync** and disables this field if PagerDuty doesn't expose a usable timestamp on the object.
       
    3. Click **Save**.
       
12. Optional. Configure field-level data protection by expanding an object and choosing how to handle each field:
    
    - **Replicate as is**: Data values at the source replicate identically to the destination.
    - **Hash**: Hash sensitive data values in the field before syncing to your destination.
    
    Workato recommends hashing personally identifiable information (PII) and other sensitive fields. Refer to [Sensitive data handling](#sensitive-data-handling) for a list of fields that commonly contain PII.
    
13. Click **Add object** again to add more objects. Repeat this step to include additional PagerDuty objects in your pipeline.
    
14. Use the **Choose how to handle schema changes** drop-down menu to select a schema drift handling option:
    
    - **Auto-sync new fields**: Automatically detects and syncs new fields added in the source.
    - **Block new fields**: Keeps the schema fixed after the pipeline starts. You must add new fields manually.
15. Optional. Enter a value in the **Concurrency limit** field to cap the number of concurrent operations. Leave the field blank to use the default limit set by Workato. The maximum value is `10`.
    
16. Choose either a standard time-based schedule or define a custom cron expression in the **Frequency** field. This determines how often the pipeline syncs data from PagerDuty to the destination.
    
    **Time-based schedule**
    
    1. Select the **Time unit**, such as **Minutes**, **Hours**, or **Days**.
       
    2. Specify the sync interval in the **Trigger every** field.
       
       For example, if you select **Hours** as the **Time unit** and enter **6** in the **Trigger every** field, the pipeline syncs every 6 hours. The minimum interval you can set is 15 minutes.
       
    3. Select a start date for the historical data sync in the **When first started, this pipeline should pick up records from** field. This defines the earliest date from which the pipeline extracts records. The pipeline picks up all available records from the source if you leave this field blank.
       
       You can't change this value after you run the pipeline.
       
    4. Click **Save** to save your progress before you [configure your data pipeline destination](/en/data-orchestration/data-pipeline-recipe/configure-pipeline-destinations#configure‒how‒data‒is‒loaded‒in‒the‒workato‒data‒pipeline).
       
    
    **Cron-based scheduling**
    
    1. Use the **Time unit** drop-down menu to select **Custom schedule**.
       
    2. Enter an expression in the **Cron expression** field using the format:
       
       ```text
       [minute] [hour] [day of month] [month] [day of week]
       ```
       
       The minimum interval for cron schedules is 15 minutes. For example, enter the following expression to sync every day at 8:00 AM UTC:
       
       ```text
       0 8 * * *
       ```
       
    3. Optional. Select a **Timezone** for the cron expression. Leave blank to use `Etc/UTC`.
       
    4. Select a start date for the historical data sync in the **When first started, this pipeline should pick up records from** field. This defines the earliest date from which the pipeline extracts records. The pipeline picks up all available records from the source if you leave this field blank.
       
       You can't change this value after you run the pipeline.
       
    5. Click **Save** to save your progress before you [configure your data pipeline destination](/en/data-orchestration/data-pipeline-recipe/configure-pipeline-destinations#configure‒how‒data‒is‒loaded‒in‒the‒workato‒data‒pipeline).
       
    

## Supported PagerDuty objects

PagerDuty data pipelines sync data from PagerDuty REST API v2 resources. The following tables list the supported objects, grouped by category. Each object syncs as a separate table in your destination:

### Incident data

| Object | Sync modes | Delete tracking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Incidents` | Full sync, incremental | No |
| `Incident Log Entries` | Full sync, incremental | No |
| `Incident Alerts` | Syncs with the parent `Incidents` object | No |
| `Incident Notes` | Syncs with the parent `Incidents` object | No |
| `Incident Status Updates` | Syncs with the parent `Incidents` object | No |

`Incident Status Updates` requires the `subscribers_status_updates` account ability, available on PagerDuty plans that include stakeholder management. Accounts without this ability don't see `Incident Status Updates` in the **Add new objects** panel.

### Services and teams

| Object | Sync modes | Delete tracking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Services` | Full sync | No |
| `Service Integrations` | Syncs with the parent `Services` object | No |
| `Teams` | Full sync | No |
| `Team Members` | Syncs with the parent `Teams` object | No |

Accounts without the `teams` PagerDuty account ability don't see `Teams` or `Team Members` in the **Add new objects** panel.

### Users

| Object | Sync modes | Delete tracking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Users` | Full sync | No |
| `User Contact Methods` | Syncs with the parent `Users` object | No |
| `User Notification Rules` | Syncs with the parent `Users` object | No |

### On-call management

| Object | Sync modes | Delete tracking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Escalation Policies` | Full sync | No |
| `Schedules` | Full sync | No |
| `Schedule Overrides` | Syncs with the parent `Schedules` object | No |
| `On Calls` | Append-only | N/A |

`On Calls` stores a daily snapshot of on-call assignments rather than a change history. Refer to [Append-only sync](#append-only-sync) and [Synthetic columns](#synthetic-columns) for more information.

### Reference and configuration data

| Object | Sync modes | Delete tracking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Priorities` | Full sync | No |
| `Vendors` | Full sync | No |
| `Tags` | Full sync | No |
| `Business Services` | Full sync | No |
| `Incident Workflows` | Full sync | No |

`Incident Workflows` requires the `incident_workflows` account ability. PagerDuty offers `Incident Workflows` on Business and Enterprise plans, with limited availability on Professional plans. Accounts without this ability don't see `Incident Workflows` in the **Add new objects** panel. `Incident Workflows` replaces PagerDuty's deprecated Response Plays object.

`Business Services` isn't gated by an account ability. The sync fails if you add `Business Services` to your pipeline on a plan that doesn't include the feature. Remove the object from your pipeline or upgrade your PagerDuty plan.

### Audit and analytics

| Object | Sync modes | Delete tracking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Audit Records` | Full sync, incremental | No |
| `Analytics Raw Incidents` | Full sync, incremental | No |
| `Analytics Metrics Incidents` | Full sync | No |

`Analytics Raw Incidents` and `Analytics Metrics Incidents` each require one of the `analytics_recommendations` or `mobile_analytics` account abilities, available on Business plans and higher. Accounts without either ability don't see these objects in the **Add new objects** panel.

`Audit Records` isn't gated by an account ability. The sync fails if you add `Audit Records` to your pipeline on a plan that doesn't include audit access. Remove the object from your pipeline or upgrade your PagerDuty plan. Refer to [Limitations](#limitations) for retention and aggregation details.

## Sync modes

PagerDuty data pipelines support full sync, incremental sync, and append-only sync. The sync mode is configured for each object when you add it to your pipeline.

### Full sync

A full sync reads all available records from PagerDuty for the selected object on every run. PagerDuty reference and configuration objects, such as `Services`, `Users`, and `Escalation Policies`, sync with full sync because PagerDuty doesn't expose a change cursor for them.

Objects with a primary key merge into the existing destination table, so records deleted in PagerDuty stay in the table. Objects without a primary key overwrite the destination table on every run.

### Incremental sync

Incremental sync extracts only records created after the previous sync, using each object's `created_at` timestamp as the cursor. The pipeline also periodically widens its sync window for `Incidents` and its child objects to recheck older records, because incidents can change status after they're created. By default, the pipeline rechecks the past `180` days every `7` days to capture status changes that a `created_at` cursor alone would miss. `Audit Records` uses the `execution_time` timestamp as its cursor. `Analytics Raw Incidents` filters its request body using `created_at`.

Refer to the [Supported objects](#supported-objects) tables to see which objects support incremental sync.

### Append-only sync

`On Calls` is a point-in-time snapshot of on-call assignments rather than a change feed. Each run appends a new snapshot to the destination without modifying or removing rows written by previous runs.

## Schema and data type handling

The following considerations apply to schema and data types when you sync data from PagerDuty:

### Nested objects and arrays

PagerDuty returns several fields as nested JSON objects or arrays, such as `Incidents.custom_fields`, `Escalation Policies.escalation_rules`, and `Schedules.schedule_layers`. Workato stores these fields as JSON columns in the destination rather than flattening them into individual columns.

Workato syncs JSON fields to the destination's native JSON type, such as `VARIANT` in Snowflake. Workato serializes JSON fields as strings if the destination doesn't support a native JSON type.

### Incident custom fields

PagerDuty accounts on a Business or Enterprise plan can define custom fields on `Incidents`. Workato retrieves each incident's custom field values and populates them in the `custom_fields` column. Incidents without any populated custom field values sync with an empty `custom_fields` value.

### Timestamps

PagerDuty returns timestamps as ISO 8601 strings with either a `Z` suffix or a numeric offset, such as `2024-01-15T10:30:00Z` or `2024-01-15T02:30:00-08:00`. Workato syncs these fields as timezone-aware timestamp columns, retaining the original offset and value from PagerDuty.

### Synthetic columns

Workato adds the following synthetic column to the destination table for `On Calls`:

| Column | Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `snapshot_date` | Date | Records the day the pipeline captured the `On Calls` snapshot. `On Calls` doesn't otherwise carry a per-record timestamp. |

## Sensitive data handling

PagerDuty objects can contain significant personally identifiable information (PII). The following objects commonly contain sensitive fields:

| Object | Sensitive fields |
| --- | --- |
| `Users` | `name`, `email`, `job_title`, `description` |
| `User Contact Methods` | `address` (phone number or email address) |
| `Incidents` | `title`, `description` (may contain system error messages or embedded user data) |
| `Incident Alerts` | `body_details`, `body_contexts` (unstructured monitoring payload that can contain server names, IP addresses, or credentials if the source integration is misconfigured) |
| `Incident Log Entries` | `channel`, `notification_data` (notification recipient and message content) |
| `Incident Notes` | `content` (free-text notes added by responders) |
| `Incident Status Updates` | `message` (free-text stakeholder update) |
| `Audit Records` | `actor_id`, `actor_type`, `details` (link account activity to a specific user and describe the change made) |

Use the **Hash** option in field-level data protection during pipeline configuration to protect PII before it reaches your destination. Refer to the [Configure the pipeline](#configure-the-pipeline) steps for more information.

## PagerDuty limitations

The following limitations apply when you use PagerDuty as a data pipeline source:

### Plan-gated objects

PagerDuty gates `Teams`, `Team Members`, `Incident Status Updates`, `Incident Workflows`, `Analytics Raw Incidents`, and `Analytics Metrics Incidents` behind account abilities that vary by plan. These objects don't appear in the **Add new objects** panel if your account doesn't have the required ability.

`Audit Records` and `Business Services` aren't gated by an account ability. The sync fails if you add either object to your pipeline without a PagerDuty plan that includes it. Remove the object from your pipeline or upgrade your PagerDuty plan.

### Audit Records retention

PagerDuty retains audit records for `12` months. The pipeline restarts the `Audit Records` sync from `12` months in the past if a paused pipeline's last successful sync is older than `12` months, because older records are no longer available from the API.

### Analytics Raw Incidents retention

PagerDuty retains raw incident analytics for `3` years. Records older than `3` years aren't available to sync.

### Analytics Metrics Incidents dimensions

`Analytics Metrics Incidents` aggregates data by the `services` and `teams` dimensions only. PagerDuty's API doesn't expose an equivalent `escalation_policies` aggregation.

### Minimum sync frequency

The minimum supported sync interval is 15 minutes.

# Configure Pendo as a data pipeline source

Set up Pendo as a data pipeline source to extract and sync product analytics records, such as visitors, accounts, guides, and usage events, to your destination.

Use this guide to set up a connection, configure your pipeline, add objects, review sync behavior, and understand known limitations.

## Pendo features supported

The following features are supported when you use Pendo as a pipeline source:

- **Cloud connectivity**: Connect to the Pendo API over HTTPS. On-prem agents aren't required.
- **Regional data centers**: Connect to Pendo subscriptions hosted in the US, US1, EU, Japan, or Australia data centers.
- **Full sync**: All objects sync in full sync mode. Refer to [Sync modes](#sync-modes) for more information.
- **Object-level selection**: Select Pendo objects to sync as separate tables in your destination. Refer to [Supported objects](#supported-objects) for the full list.
- **Delete tracking**: Detect deleted records for objects that have a primary key. Refer to [Delete tracking](#delete-tracking) for more information.
- **Custom field discovery**: Automatically syncs visitor and account metadata fields, including custom fields. Refer to [Visitor and account metadata fields](#visitor-and-account-metadata-fields) for more information.
- **Schema drift detection and handling**: Detect and apply schema changes automatically with **Auto-sync new fields**, or keep the schema fixed with **Block new fields**.
- **Field-level data protection**: Hash or replicate sensitive fields as is before the data reaches your destination.
- **Configurable sync frequency**: Schedule syncs on a time-based interval or with a cron expression. The minimum supported interval is `15` minutes.

## Pendo prerequisites

Connecting Pendo as a data pipeline source requires:

- A Pendo subscription with integration keys enabled. Pendo subscription admins can enable this feature.
- A Pendo integration key with **Allow Write Access** enabled. You must have Pendo subscription admin permissions and integration key access to create a key. Refer to the Pendo [integration keys](https://support.pendo.io/hc/en-us/articles/9491198203547-Pendo-integration-keys) documentation for setup steps.
- The region that hosts your Pendo subscription

> **REQUIRED PERMISSIONS**
> 
> The integration key must have **Allow Write Access** enabled. Pendo requires this setting for Aggregation API queries, which the connector uses to read visitors, accounts, applications, product areas, and events. The connector only reads data and never writes to your Pendo subscription.

## Supported connection types

Pendo data pipelines support one authentication method:

- **Integration key**: Provide a Pendo integration key and the region that hosts your Pendo subscription. Refer to [Prerequisites](#prerequisites) for setup requirements.

## Connect to Pendo

Complete the following steps to connect Pendo as a data pipeline source:

Connect to Pendo

1. Select **Create > Connection** or press C twice.
   
2. Search for `Pendo` and select it as your app.
   
3. Enter a name in the **Connection name** field.
   
4. Use the **Location** drop-down menu to select the project where you plan to store the connection.
   
5. Use the **Region** drop-down menu to select the region that hosts your Pendo subscription. The region must match the URL you use to sign in to Pendo. For example, select the EU region if you sign in at `app.eu.pendo.io`.
   
6. Paste your Pendo integration key into the **Integration Key** field.
   
7. Select **Connect** to verify and save the connection. Workato displays a success message when the connection is established.
   

## Configure the pipeline

Complete the following steps to configure Pendo as your data pipeline source:

1. Select **Create > Data pipeline** or press C+I.
   
2. Enter a name for the data pipeline in the **Data pipeline name** field.
   
   ![Data pipeline setup](/assets/set-up-pipeline.Cxx6hIk2.png)_Data pipeline setup_
   
3. Use the **Location** drop-down menu to select the project where you plan to store the data pipeline.
   
4. Click **Start building**.
   
5. Click the **Extract new/updated records from source app** trigger. This trigger defines how the pipeline retrieves data from Pendo.
   
   ![Configure the Extract new/updated records from source app trigger](/assets/choose-source-app.B2OOUpgY.png)_Configure the Extract new/updated records from source app trigger_
   
6. Use the **Your Connected Source Apps** drop-down menu to select **Pendo**.
   
7. Choose the Pendo connection you plan to use for this pipeline. Alternatively, click **\+ New connection** to create a new connection.
   
8. Click **Add object** to open the **Add new objects** panel.
   
   ![Add objects](/assets/add-objects-pendo.CDU67w48.png)_Add objects_
   
9. Search or browse the list of available Pendo objects, select the objects you plan to sync, and click **Add**.
   
   All Pendo objects appear with a **Full sync** tag in the object list. Refer to [Sync modes](#sync-modes) for more information.
   
10. Review and customize the schema for each selected object. The pipeline automatically fetches an object's schema when you select it. This ensures the destination matches the source.
    
    Expand an object to view associated fields. Keep all fields selected to extract all available data, or deselect specific fields to exclude them from data extraction and schema replication.
    
11. Optional. Configure field-level data protection by expanding an object and choosing how to handle each field:
    
    - **Replicate as is**: Data values at the source replicate identically to the destination.
    - **Hash**: Hash sensitive data values in the field before syncing to your destination.
    
    Workato recommends hashing personally identifiable information (PII) and other sensitive fields. Refer to [Sensitive data handling](#sensitive-data-handling) for a list of fields that commonly contain PII.
    
12. Click **Add object** again to add more objects. Repeat this step to include additional Pendo objects in your pipeline.
    
13. Use the **Choose how to handle schema changes** drop-down menu to select a schema drift handling option:
    
    - **Auto-sync new fields**: Automatically detects and syncs new fields added in the source.
    - **Block new fields**: Keeps the schema fixed after the pipeline starts. You must add new fields manually. This option may cause the destination to fall out of sync if the source schema updates.
    
    Refer to [Schema replication and schema drift management](/en/data-orchestration/data-pipeline-recipe/concepts#schema-drift) for more information.
    
    Workato recommends **Auto-sync new fields** for Pendo subscriptions that use custom visitor or account metadata, so new metadata fields sync automatically. Refer to [Visitor and account metadata fields](#visitor-and-account-metadata-fields) for more information.
    
14. Optional. Enter a value in the **Concurrency limit** field to cap the number of concurrent operations. Leave the field blank to use the default limit set by Workato. The maximum value is `100`.
    
15. Choose either a standard time-based schedule or define a custom cron expression in the **Frequency** field. This determines how often the pipeline syncs data from Pendo to the destination.
    
    **Time-based schedule**
    
    1. Select the **Time unit**, such as **Minutes**, **Hours**, or **Days**.
       
    2. Specify the sync interval in the **Trigger every** field.
       
       For example, the pipeline syncs every 6 hours if you select **Hours** as the **Time unit** and enter `6` in the **Trigger every** field.
       
       The minimum interval you can set is `15` minutes.
       
    3. Optional. Select a start date in the **When first started, this pipeline should pick up records from** field. This setting applies to event objects and the event-based `Visitor Application` and `Account Application` objects. If you leave it blank, these objects extract the most recent `91` complete UTC days. Other Pendo objects ignore this setting.
       
       You can't change this value after you run the pipeline.
       
    4. Click **Save** to save your progress before you [configure your data pipeline destination](/en/data-orchestration/data-pipeline-recipe/configure-pipeline-destinations#configure‒how‒data‒is‒loaded‒in‒the‒workato‒data‒pipeline).
       
    
    **Cron-based scheduling**
    
    1. Use the **Time unit** drop-down menu to select **Custom schedule**.
       
    2. Enter an expression in the **Cron expression** field using the format:
       
       ```text
       [minute] [hour] [day of month] [month] [day of week]
       ```
       
       The minimum interval for cron schedules is `15` minutes.
       
       For example, enter the following expression to sync every day at 8:00 AM UTC:
       
       ```text
       0 8 * * *
       ```
       
    3. Optional. Select a **Timezone** for the cron expression. Leave blank to use `Etc/UTC`.
       
    4. Optional. Select a start date in the **When first started, this pipeline should pick up records from** field. This setting applies to event objects and the event-based `Visitor Application` and `Account Application` objects. If you leave it blank, these objects extract the most recent `91` complete UTC days. Other Pendo objects ignore this setting.
       
       You can't change this value after you run the pipeline.
       
    5. Click **Save** to save your progress before you [configure your data pipeline destination](/en/data-orchestration/data-pipeline-recipe/configure-pipeline-destinations#configure‒how‒data‒is‒loaded‒in‒the‒workato‒data‒pipeline).
       
    
    > **EVENT HISTORY START DATE**
    > 
    > The start date applies only to event objects, such as `Events` and `Page Events`, and the `Visitor Application` and `Account Application` objects, which are built from events. These objects extract the last `91` days of events if you leave the field blank, and events older than `91` days drop out of the destination on each run. Set a start date before the first run if you need to retain older events. Refer to [Event history window](#event-history-window) for more information.
    

## Supported Pendo objects

Pendo data pipelines sync data from the Pendo API (v1). The following tables list the supported objects, grouped by category. Each object syncs as a separate table in your destination:

### Applications, visitors, and accounts

| Object | Sync modes | Delete tracking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Applications` | Full sync | Yes (soft) |
| `Visitors` | Full sync | No |
| `Accounts` | Full sync | No |
| `Visitor Account` | Full sync | Yes |
| `Visitor Application` | Full sync | Yes |
| `Account Application` | Full sync | Yes |

`Visitor Account` links each visitor to the account IDs in its Pendo visitor metadata. `Visitor Application` and `Account Application` are built from events, so they only include pairs with at least one event in the event history window. A pair is marked as deleted when its last event leaves the window.

### Product configuration

| Object | Sync modes | Delete tracking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Pages` | Full sync | Yes |
| `Page Rule History` | Full sync | No |
| `Features` | Full sync | Yes |
| `Groups` | Full sync | Yes |
| `Guides` | Full sync | Yes |
| `Guide Step History` | Full sync | No |
| `Polls` | Full sync | No |
| `Track Types` | Full sync | Yes |
| `Segments` | Full sync | Yes |

`Groups` contains Pendo product areas. `Page Rule History` and `Polls` sync one row per page rule or guide poll, extracted from the current `Pages` and `Guides` records. `Guide Step History` syncs one row per step in every historical version of each guide.

### Events

| Object | Sync modes | Delete tracking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Events` | Full sync | No |
| `Page Events` | Full sync | No |
| `Feature Events` | Full sync | No |
| `Guide Events` | Full sync | No |
| `Poll Events` | Full sync | No |
| `Track Type Events` | Full sync | No |

Event objects extract events from complete UTC days within the event history window. Refer to [Event history window](#event-history-window) for more information.

## Sync modes

Pendo data pipelines support full sync for all objects. Incremental sync isn't available.

### Full sync

A full sync reads all available records from Pendo for the selected object on every run. Event objects and the `Visitor Application` and `Account Application` objects read all events within the event history window on every run.

Objects with a primary key merge into the existing destination table, so records deleted in Pendo stay in the table. Objects without a primary key overwrite the destination table on every run.

### Delete tracking

`Applications` supports soft delete tracking, marked **Yes (soft)** in the [Supported objects](#supported-objects) tables. Pendo returns a native `isDeleted` field on each application, and Workato reads this field to mark applications that Pendo flags as deleted in the destination.

Objects marked **Yes** in the [Supported objects](#supported-objects) tables have a primary key. Workato compares each full sync against the previous run and marks records that no longer appear in Pendo as deleted in the destination.

`Visitors`, `Accounts`, event objects, `Page Rule History`, `Polls`, and `Guide Step History` don't have a primary key, so Workato can't track individual deleted rows for these objects.

## Schema and data type handling

The following considerations apply to schema and data types when you sync data from Pendo:

### Timestamps

Pendo returns timestamps, such as `createdAt` and `lastUpdatedAt`, as Unix epoch integers in milliseconds. Workato preserves the raw integer values in the destination and doesn't convert them to a timestamp format.

### Nested objects and arrays

Pendo records can include nested objects and arrays, such as `rules` on `Pages`, `steps` and `polls` on `Guides`, `items` on `Groups`, and `definition` on `Segments`. Workato stores these as JSON string columns in the destination and doesn't flatten them into individual columns.

### Visitor and account metadata fields

Workato reads your Pendo visitor and account metadata schemas each time it fetches the schema for `Visitors` or `Accounts`. Each metadata field syncs as a separate column named `metadata_<group>_<field>`, in lowercase. Runs of characters other than letters and numbers become underscores, and leading or trailing underscores are removed. If two fields would have the same column name, Workato adds a suffix to keep them distinct. This includes custom fields and fields from other metadata groups, such as `auto` and `pendo`.

Workato maps boolean, integer, and decimal metadata fields to the matching destination types. Date, list, and other metadata field types sync as strings.

New metadata fields appear the next time Workato fetches the object schema. Select **Auto-sync new fields** when you [configure the pipeline](#configure-the-pipeline) so new fields sync automatically.

### Sensitive data handling

Pendo objects can contain personally identifiable information (PII), such as visitor identifiers, IP addresses, and location data. The following objects commonly contain sensitive fields:

| Object | Sensitive fields |
| --- | --- |
| `Visitors` | `visitorId`, metadata fields (`metadata_*`), which can include names and email addresses depending on your Pendo configuration |
| `Accounts` | `accountId`, metadata fields (`metadata_*`) |
| `Visitor Account`, `Visitor Application`, `Account Application` | `visitorId`, `accountId` |
| `Events`, `Page Events`, `Feature Events`, `Guide Events`, `Poll Events`, `Track Type Events` | `visitorId`, `accountId`, `accountIds`, `remoteIp`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `country`, `region`, `userAgent` |
| `Poll Events` | `pollResponse` |
| `Pages`, `Groups`, `Guides`, `Guide Step History`, `Segments`, `Track Types` | `createdByUser`, `lastUpdatedByUser` |

Use the **Hash** option in field-level data protection during pipeline configuration to protect PII before it reaches your destination. Refer to the [Configure the pipeline](#configure-the-pipeline) steps for more information.

## Pendo limitations

The following limitations apply when you use Pendo as a data pipeline source:

### Event history window

Event objects and the `Visitor Application` and `Account Application` objects extract events from the date set in the **When first started, this pipeline should pick up records from** field through the end of the previous UTC day. These objects extract the last `91` days of events if you leave the field blank. Events from the current UTC day sync on the next run after the day ends.

Every run is a full sync, so a blank start date produces a rolling window. Events older than `91` days drop out of the destination table on the next run. Set a start date before the first run if you need to retain older events, because you can't change the start date after the pipeline runs.

### Daily event volume

Workato extracts events one UTC day at a time and requests up to `1,000` rows per day. Pendo doesn't provide a continuation within a one-day window. If a day's response reaches the request limit, the run fails rather than risk omitting rows. This applies to event objects and the `Visitor Application` and `Account Application` objects.

### Minimum sync frequency

The minimum supported sync interval is `15` minutes.

# Configure Pipedrive as a data pipeline source

Set up Pipedrive as a data pipeline source to extract and sync CRM data, such as deals, persons, organizations, activities, and notes to your destination.

Use this guide to get a Pipedrive API token, connect Pipedrive as a data pipeline source, configure the pipeline, and understand the supported objects, sync modes, schema handling, and limitations.

## Pipedrive features supported

The following features are supported when you use Pipedrive as a pipeline source:

- **Cloud connectivity**: Connects to the Pipedrive API over HTTPS. An on-prem agent isn't required.
- **Object-level selection**: Select the supported objects you plan to sync when you configure the pipeline.
- **Sync modes**: Core CRM objects, such as `deals`, `persons`, and `activities`, support incremental sync and default to it. You can switch these objects to full sync. All other objects use full sync. Refer to [Sync modes](#sync-modes) for more information.
- **Delete tracking**: Detects deleted records for full-sync objects and for most incremental objects. Refer to [Delete tracking](#delete-tracking) for more information.
- **Custom field support**: Syncs Pipedrive custom fields in a single `custom_fields` JSON column and syncs field definitions as separate objects.
- **Schema drift detection and handling**: Detect and apply schema changes automatically with **Auto-sync new fields**, or keep the schema fixed with **Block new fields**.
- **Field-level data protection**: Hash or replicate sensitive fields as is before the data reaches your destination.
- **Configurable sync frequency**: Schedule syncs on a time-based interval or with a cron expression. The minimum supported interval is `15` minutes.

## Pipedrive prerequisites

Connecting Pipedrive as a data pipeline source requires:

- A Pipedrive account with access to the data you plan to sync.
- A Pipedrive API token. Refer to [Retrieve a Pipedrive API token](#pipedrive-setup) for steps.

> **REQUIRED PERMISSIONS**
> 
> The pipeline reads data with the permissions of the Pipedrive user who owns the API token. Use a user account with privileges to view all records for the objects you plan to sync. Some objects require elevated permissions or a Pipedrive add-on. Refer to [Plan and permission requirements](#plan-and-permission-requirements) for more information.

## Supported connection types

Pipedrive data pipelines support API token authentication:

- **API token**: Authorizes Workato to read the data that the token owner can access in Pipedrive. The token doesn't expire unless you regenerate it. Refer to [Retrieve a Pipedrive API token](#pipedrive-setup) for setup steps.

## Retrieve a Pipedrive API token

Complete the following steps to retrieve the API token for your Pipedrive user. Skip this section if you already have the API token you plan to use:

1. Click your profile icon on your Pipedrive dashboard, then click **Personal preferences**.
   
2. Select the **API** tab.
   
3. Copy and save **Your personal API token** for use in Workato.
   

Your Pipedrive permission set may not allow API access if the **API** tab doesn't appear. Refer to [Pipedrive's documentation](https://pipedrive.readme.io/docs/how-to-find-the-api-token) for more information.

> **API TOKEN REGENERATION**
> 
> Each Pipedrive user has one active API token for each Pipedrive company. A regenerated token invalidates the previous one, and pipelines that use the previous token fail until you update the connection.

## Connect to Pipedrive

Complete the following steps to connect Pipedrive as a data pipeline source:

Connect to Pipedrive

1. Click **Create > Connection** or press C twice.
   
2. Search for `Pipedrive` and select it as your app.
   
3. Enter a name for your connection in the **Connection name** field.
   
   ![Pipedrive connection](/assets/pipedrive-connection-setup.CKOYaeNm.png)_Pipedrive connection_
   
4. Use the **Location** drop-down menu to select the project where you plan to store the connection.
   
5. Enter the **API token**. Refer to [Retrieve the API token](#pipedrive-setup) for more information.
   
6. Click **Connect**.
   

## Configure the pipeline

Complete the following steps to configure Pipedrive as your data pipeline source:

1. Select **Create > Data pipeline** or press C+I.
   
2. Enter a name for the data pipeline in the **Data pipeline name** field.
   
   ![Data pipeline setup](/assets/set-up-pipeline.Cxx6hIk2.png)_Data pipeline setup_
   
3. Use the **Location** drop-down menu to select the project where you plan to store the data pipeline.
   
4. Click **Start building**.
   
5. Click the **Extract new/updated records from source app** trigger. This trigger defines how the pipeline retrieves data from Pipedrive.
   
   ![Configure the Extract new/updated records from source app trigger](/assets/choose-source-app.B2OOUpgY.png)_Configure the Extract new/updated records from source app trigger_
   
6. Use the **Your Connected Source Apps** drop-down menu to select **Pipedrive**.
   
7. Choose the Pipedrive connection you plan to use for this pipeline. Alternatively, click **\+ New connection** to create a new connection.
   
8. Click **Add object** to open the **Add new objects** panel.
   
   ![Add objects](/assets/add-objects-pipedrive.DosoryLr.png)_Add objects_
   
9. Search or browse the list of available Pipedrive objects, select the objects you plan to sync, and click **Add**.
   
   > **OBJECTS WITH EXTRA REQUIREMENTS**
   > 
   > Some objects consume more of your Pipedrive API budget or require a Pipedrive add-on. Refer to [Per-deal requests](#per-deal-requests) and [Plan and permission requirements](#plan-and-permission-requirements) before you select `deal_products`, `deal_participants`, `projects`, or `tasks`.
   
10. Review and customize the schema for each selected object. The pipeline automatically fetches an object's schema when you select it. This ensures the destination matches the source.
    
    Expand an object to view associated fields. Keep all fields selected to extract all available data, or deselect specific fields to exclude them from data extraction and schema replication.
    
11. Optional. Click the **Settings** (gear) icon next to the object to configure the sync mode:
    
    12
    
    Click the **Settings** (gear) icon next to the object.
    
    13
    
    Select a **Sync mode**:
    
    - **Incremental**: Sync only records created or updated since the previous run.
    - **Full sync**: Reload all records on each run.
    
    Workato disables this field for objects that only support full sync.
    
    14
    
    Click **Save**.
    
12. Click the **Settings** (gear) icon next to the object.
    
13. Select a **Sync mode**:
    
    - **Incremental**: Sync only records created or updated since the previous run.
    - **Full sync**: Reload all records on each run.
    
    Workato disables this field for objects that only support full sync.
    
14. Click **Save**.
    
15. Optional. Configure field-level data protection by expanding an object and choosing how to handle each field:
    
    - **Replicate as is**: Data values at the source replicate identically to the destination.
    - **Hash**: Hash sensitive data values in the field before syncing to your destination.
    
    Workato recommends hashing personally identifiable information (PII) and other sensitive fields. Refer to [Sensitive data handling](#sensitive-data-handling) for a list of fields that commonly contain PII.
    
16. Click **Add object** again to add more objects. Repeat this step to include additional Pipedrive objects in your pipeline.
    
17. Use the **Choose how to handle schema changes** drop-down menu to select a schema drift handling option:
    
    - **Auto-sync new fields**: Automatically detects and syncs new fields added in the source.
    - **Block new fields**: Keeps the schema fixed after the pipeline starts. You must add new fields manually. This option may cause the destination to fall out of sync if the source schema updates.
    
    Refer to [Schema replication and schema drift management](/en/data-orchestration/data-pipeline-recipe/concepts#schema-drift) for more information.
    
18. Choose either a standard time-based schedule or define a custom cron expression in the **Frequency** field. This determines how often the pipeline syncs data from Pipedrive to the destination.
    
    **Time-based schedule**
    
    1. Select the **Time unit**, such as **Minutes**, **Hours**, or **Days**.
       
    2. Specify the sync interval in the **Trigger every** field.
       
       For example, the pipeline syncs every 6 hours if you select **Hours** as the **Time unit** and enter `6` in the **Trigger every** field.
       
       The minimum interval you can set is 15 minutes.
       
    3. Select a start date for the historical data sync in the **When first started, this pipeline should pick up records from** field. This defines the earliest date from which the pipeline extracts records. The pipeline picks up all available records from the source if you leave this field blank.
       
       You can't change this value after you run the pipeline.
       
    4. Click **Save** to save your progress before you [configure your data pipeline destination](/en/data-orchestration/data-pipeline-recipe/configure-pipeline-destinations#configure‒how‒data‒is‒loaded‒in‒the‒workato‒data‒pipeline).
       
    
    **Cron-based scheduling**
    
    1. Use the **Time unit** drop-down menu to select **Custom schedule**.
       
    2. Enter an expression in the **Cron expression** field using the format:
       
       ```text
       [minute] [hour] [day of month] [month] [day of week]
       ```
       
       The minimum interval for cron schedules is 15 minutes.
       
       For example, enter the following expression to sync every day at 8:00 AM UTC:
       
       ```text
       0 8 * * *
       ```
       
    3. Optional. Select a **Timezone** for the cron expression. Leave blank to use `Etc/UTC`.
       
    4. Select a start date for the historical data sync in the **When first started, this pipeline should pick up records from** field. This defines the earliest date from which the pipeline extracts records. The pipeline picks up all available records from the source if you leave this field blank.
       
       You can't change this value after you run the pipeline.
       
    5. Click **Save** to save your progress before you [configure your data pipeline destination](/en/data-orchestration/data-pipeline-recipe/configure-pipeline-destinations#configure‒how‒data‒is‒loaded‒in‒the‒workato‒data‒pipeline).
       
    
    > **HISTORICAL START DATE**
    > 
    > The historical start date applies only to objects that support incremental sync. Objects that only support full sync extract all available records. Refer to [Supported objects](#supported-objects) to view the sync modes for each object.
    

## Supported Pipedrive objects

Pipedrive data pipelines sync data from the Pipedrive API. The following tables list the supported objects, grouped by category. Each object syncs as a separate table in your destination and appears in the pipeline builder as **Label (object\_name)**, such as **Persons (persons)**. The sync mode column shows the modes an object supports. Incremental is the default for objects that support it. Pipedrive custom object types aren't supported.

### Deals

The following objects describe deals and associated products and persons:

| Object | Sync mode | Delete tracking | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `deals` | Full sync, incremental | Yes (soft) | Excludes archived deals. Refer to `deal_archived`. |
| `deal_archived` | Full sync | Yes | Deals archived in Pipedrive. |
| `deal_products` | Full sync | Yes | Products attached to each deal. Makes at least one request per deal on every sync. |
| `deal_participants` | Full sync | Yes | Persons associated with each deal. Makes at least one request per deal on every sync. |

### Persons and organizations

The following objects describe the contacts and companies in your Pipedrive account:

| Object | Sync mode | Delete tracking | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `persons` | Full sync, incremental | Yes (soft) | The `emails` and `phones` fields sync as JSON columns. Contains PII. |
| `organizations` | Full sync, incremental | Yes (soft) | Contains PII. |

### Leads

The following objects describe leads and their supporting definitions:

| Object | Sync mode | Delete tracking | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `leads` | Full sync, incremental | No | Excludes archived leads. Refer to `lead_archived`. |
| `lead_archived` | Full sync | Yes | Leads archived in Pipedrive. |
| `lead_labels` | Full sync | Yes | Lead label definitions. |
| `lead_sources` | Full sync | Yes | Lead source definitions. |

### Activities, notes, and files

The following objects describe the work logged against deals, persons, and organizations:

| Object | Sync mode | Delete tracking | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `activities` | Full sync, incremental | Yes (soft) | Contains PII. |
| `activity_types` | Full sync | Yes | Activity type definitions, such as call, meeting, and email. |
| `notes` | Full sync, incremental | Yes (soft) | Free-text notes attached to deals, persons, organizations, and leads. Contains PII. |
| `files` | Full sync, incremental | Yes (soft) | File metadata only. File content doesn't sync. |

### Products

The following object describes the products in your Pipedrive product catalog:

| Object | Sync mode | Delete tracking | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `products` | Full sync, incremental | Yes (soft) | Product catalog records. |

### Pipelines and account configuration

The following objects describe pipeline stages, users, and account-level settings:

| Object | Sync mode | Delete tracking | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pipelines` | Full sync | Yes | Sales pipeline definitions. |
| `stages` | Full sync | Yes | Stage definitions for each pipeline. |
| `users` | Full sync, incremental | Yes (soft) | Use to resolve `owner_id` values on other objects. Contains PII. |
| `roles` | Full sync | Yes | Permission role definitions. Might require elevated permissions. |
| `goals` | Full sync | Yes | Goal definitions. |
| `currencies` | Full sync | Yes | Currencies supported by your account. |
| `filters` | Full sync | Yes | Saved filter definitions. |

### Field definitions

The following objects describe the standard and custom fields in your Pipedrive account. Use these fields to resolve the keys in the `custom_fields` column to field names and types. Refer to [Custom fields](#custom-fields) for more information:

| Object | Sync mode | Delete tracking | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `deal_fields` | Full sync | Yes | Field definitions for `deals`, `deal_archived`, `leads`, and `lead_archived`. |
| `person_fields` | Full sync | Yes | Field definitions for `persons`. |
| `organization_fields` | Full sync | Yes | Field definitions for `organizations`. |
| `activity_fields` | Full sync | Yes | Field definitions for `activities`. |
| `product_fields` | Full sync | Yes | Field definitions for `products`. |
| `note_fields` | Full sync | Yes | Field definitions for `notes`. |

### Projects

The following objects require the Pipedrive Projects add-on. Refer to [Plan and permission requirements](#plan-and-permission-requirements) for more information:

| Object | Sync mode | Delete tracking | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projects` | Full sync | Yes | Requires the Projects add-on. |
| `tasks` | Full sync | Yes | Requires the Projects add-on. |

## Sync modes

Pipedrive data pipelines support full sync and incremental sync. The sync mode is configured per object when you add it to your pipeline. Objects that support incremental sync default to it.

### Full sync

A full sync reads all available records from Pipedrive for the selected object on every run. Incremental objects read only records since the historical start date if you set one. Objects without an incremental filter, such as field definitions, pipelines, and archived deals and leads, use full sync. Incremental objects also use full sync for their first run. You can switch an incremental object to full sync if you need a complete extraction on each run.

Objects with a primary key merge into the existing destination table, so records deleted in Pipedrive stay in the table. Objects without a primary key overwrite the destination table on every run.

### Incremental sync

Incremental sync reads only the records created or updated since the previous run. Incremental objects use the `update_time` field as the cursor, except `users`, which uses `modified`. The `users` and `files` objects read changes from Pipedrive's recent-changes history, which covers approximately `30` days. Refer to [Change history window](#change-history-window) for more information.

Refer to the [Supported objects](#supported-objects) tables to see the sync mode for each object.

### Delete tracking

Delete tracking is per-object and follows sync mode:

- **Full-sync objects**: Workato compares each full sync against the previous run and marks records that no longer exist in Pipedrive as deleted in your destination. Deletions are detected on the next full sync.
- **Incremental objects**: Pipedrive reports deletions for `deals`, `persons`, `organizations`, `activities`, `products`, `notes`, `files`, and `users`. Workato marks these records as deleted in your destination. The marker column depends on the object. Refer to [Synthetic columns](#synthetic-columns) for more information.
- **Leads**: Pipedrive doesn't report deleted leads, so Workato can't detect them while `leads` syncs incrementally. Deleted leads stay in your destination. Switch `leads` to full sync to detect deletions.

Delete tracking follows the full-sync behavior if you switch an incremental object to full sync.

Incremental delete tracking depends on Pipedrive's recent-changes history, which covers approximately 30 days. Refer to [Change history window](#change-history-window) for more information.

## Schema and data type handling

The following considerations apply to schema and data types when you sync data from Pipedrive:

### Custom fields

Pipedrive supports user-defined custom fields. The `deals`, `deal_archived`, `persons`, `organizations`, `products`, `leads`, and `lead_archived` objects store custom field values in a single `custom_fields` JSON column. Adding a custom field in Pipedrive doesn't change the table schema, because the column holds all custom field values.

Each key in the `custom_fields` JSON is a 40-character hash. Join the key with the `field_code` column in the matching field-definition object to resolve it to a field name and type:

| Object | Field-definition object |
| --- | --- |
| `deals`, `deal_archived`, `leads`, `lead_archived` | `deal_fields` |
| `persons` | `person_fields` |
| `organizations` | `organization_fields` |
| `products` | `product_fields` |

### Nested fields and data types

Nested objects and arrays, such as `label_ids`, `emails`, and `phones`, sync as JSON strings. Decimal fields, such as `value` on `deals`, sync with a precision of `28` and a scale of `12`.

### Synthetic columns

Workato adds the following columns to destination tables for objects that support soft deletes:

| Column | Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `_workato_is_deleted` | Boolean | Set to `true` for records deleted in Pipedrive. Present on `persons`, `organizations`, `activities`, `notes`, `files`, and `products`. |
| `deleted` | Boolean | Set to `true` for deals deleted in Pipedrive. Present on `deals`, alongside the `is_deleted` field from Pipedrive. |

The `users` object uses the `is_deleted` field from Pipedrive to mark deleted users.

## Sensitive data handling

Pipedrive objects can contain significant personally identifiable information (PII). The following objects commonly contain sensitive fields:

| Object | Sensitive fields |
| --- | --- |
| `persons` | `name`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `emails`, `phones`, `birthday`, and the `postal_address` fields |
| `organizations` | `name` and the `address` fields |
| `activities` | `subject`, `note`, and the `location` fields |
| `notes` | `content` |
| `deals` | `title` |
| `users` | `name`, `email`, and `phone` |

The `content` field on `notes` and the `note` field on `activities` are free text and carry the highest risk, because users can enter any personal information. Custom fields are defined by your organization and can also contain PII, so review the `custom_fields` column on the objects that include it.

Use the **Hash** option in field-level data protection during pipeline configuration to protect PII before it reaches your destination. Refer to the [Configure the pipeline](#configure-the-pipeline) steps for more information.

## Pipedrive limitations

The following limitations apply when you use Pipedrive as a data pipeline source:

### Change history window

Incremental sync for `users` and `files` and delete tracking for `deals`, `persons`, `organizations`, `activities`, `products`, `notes`, `files`, and `users` rely on Pipedrive's recent-changes history, which covers approximately `30` days. The sync for these objects fails if the pipeline doesn't run for more than 30 days, because Pipedrive no longer provides the changes and deletions made during the gap.

Use **Re-sync** on the affected object to recover. A re-sync extracts the object in full, which clears the error. Refer to [View synced objects and statuses](/en/data-orchestration/data-pipeline-recipe/monitor#view-synced-objects-and-statuses) for more information.

### Deleted leads aren't detected

Pipedrive doesn't report deleted leads, and `leads` syncs incrementally by default. Deleted leads stay in your destination. Switch `leads` to full sync if you need Workato to detect deleted leads.

### Rate limits

Pipedrive limits API usage with a daily token budget and a burst limit for each API token. Each request consumes tokens from the budget. The daily budget is `30,000` tokens multiplied by your plan multiplier and the number of seats in your Pipedrive account. All API usage in the account shares the budget.

| Pipedrive plan | Daily token budget (1 seat) | Burst limit for API tokens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lite | `30,000` | `20` requests every 2 seconds |
| Growth | `60,000` | `40` requests every 2 seconds |
| Premium | `150,000` | `100` requests every 2 seconds |
| Ultimate | `210,000` | `120` requests every 2 seconds |

The pipeline waits and retries automatically when it reaches the burst limit. The sync fails if the daily budget is exhausted, and you can retry after Pipedrive resets the budget. Reduce the number of selected objects, increase the sync interval, or upgrade your Pipedrive plan to stay within the budget.

Refer to the [Pipedrive rate limiting documentation](https://pipedrive.readme.io/docs/core-api-concepts-rate-limiting) for more information.

### Per-deal requests

The `deal_products` and `deal_participants` objects make at least one request per deal on every sync, because Pipedrive returns these objects for each deal. The request count grows with the number of deals in your account and consumes your daily token budget. Select these objects only if needed, and sync the objects on a separate pipeline if your account has a large number of deals.

### Plan and permission requirements

Certain objects require a Pipedrive add-on or additional permissions:

| Object | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| `projects`, `tasks` | The Pipedrive Projects add-on |
| `roles` | A Pipedrive user with elevated permissions |

The sync for an object fails with a permission error if the API token owner doesn't have access to it. Pipedrive returns only the records the token owner can view for all other objects, so users with restricted permission sets might see fewer records than exist in your account.

### File content isn't synced

The `files` object syncs file metadata, such as the file name and size, and doesn't sync file content.

### Minimum sync frequency

The minimum supported sync interval is `15` minutes. You can't trigger syncs more frequently than this.
