# Configure SurveyMonkey as a data pipeline source

Set up SurveyMonkey as a data pipeline source to extract surveys, survey structure, responses, answers, and collectors into your destination.

Use this guide to set up a connection, configure your pipeline, add objects, review sync behavior, and understand known limitations.

## Features supported

The following features are supported when you use SurveyMonkey as a pipeline source:

- **Cloud connectivity**: Connect to SurveyMonkey over HTTPS through the API host for your account's data center. On-prem agents aren't required.
- **Full sync and incremental sync**: Supports full sync for every object and incremental sync for `surveys`, `survey_responses`, and `collectors`. Refer to [Sync modes](#sync-modes) for more information.
- **Object-level selection**: Select from SurveyMonkey objects, including surveys, survey structure, responses, answers, and collectors, to sync as separate tables in your destination. Refer to [Supported objects](#supported-objects) for the full list.
- **Delete tracking**: Detect deleted records on full-sync objects and deleted questions in `survey_questions`. Refer to [Delete tracking](#delete-tracking) for more information.
- **Schema drift detection and handling**: Detect and apply schema changes automatically with **Auto-sync new fields**, or keep the schema fixed with **Block new fields**.
- **Field-level data protection**: Hash or replicate sensitive fields as is before the data reaches your destination.
- **Configurable sync frequency**: Schedule syncs on a time-based interval or with a cron expression. The minimum supported interval is `15` minutes.

## Prerequisites

Connecting SurveyMonkey as a data pipeline source requires:

- A SurveyMonkey account. You need a paid plan to sync `survey_responses` and `response_answers`. Refer to [Responses require a paid plan](#responses-require-a-paid-plan) for more information.
- SurveyMonkey account credentials to authorize the OAuth 2.0 connection. Workato recommends using an admin account to avoid permission issues.
- A [custom OAuth profile](/en/custom-oauth-profiles), if your SurveyMonkey account is hosted in a data center outside the United States.

> **REQUIRED SCOPES**
> 
> The SurveyMonkey app behind a custom OAuth profile must grant the `users_read`, `surveys_read`, `collectors_read`, `responses_read`, and `responses_read_detail` scopes. Add the `contacts_read` scope to sync your account's contact field labels as the column labels for the `collector_recipients` custom field columns.

## Supported connection types

SurveyMonkey data pipelines support OAuth 2.0 authentication. You sign in to SurveyMonkey and authorize Workato to read your account data. Use a custom OAuth profile to authorize through your own SurveyMonkey app or to connect to a data center outside the United States.

> **DRAFT APPS AREN'T SUITABLE FOR DATA PIPELINES**
> 
> SurveyMonkey limits apps in draft state to a low number of API requests per day. A data pipeline makes many requests on every run, so a custom OAuth profile based on a draft app is likely to reach the daily limit and fail. Refer to the SurveyMonkey [Request and Response Limits](https://api.surveymonkey.com/v3/docs#request-and-response-limits) guide for more information.

## Connect to SurveyMonkey

Complete the following steps to connect SurveyMonkey as a data pipeline source:

Connect to SurveyMonkey

1. Click **Create > Connection** or press C twice.
   
2. Search for `SurveyMonkey` and select it as your app.
   
3. Provide a **Connection name** that identifies which SurveyMonkey account Workato is connected to.
   
4. Use the **Location** drop-down menu to select the project or folder where you plan to store the connection.
   
5. Use the **Datacenter** drop-down menu to select the data center that hosts your SurveyMonkey account. Defaults to **United States**. You must use a [custom OAuth profile](/en/custom-oauth-profiles) to connect to a data center outside of the United States.
   
6. Optional. Use the **Custom OAuth profile** drop-down menu to select a [custom OAuth profile](/en/custom-oauth-profiles) for your connection. All requests to the app use the profile you specify here.
   
7. Click **Connect** to open the SurveyMonkey authorization window.
   
8. Sign in to SurveyMonkey with your account credentials. We recommend you use an admin account to avoid permission roadblocks.
   
9. Read the terms of service and click **Authorize** to complete the connection setup.
   
   > **VIEW ANSWERS REQUIREMENT**
   > 
   > Select `View answers along with responses` during authorization to retrieve survey response answers. The `Completed survey response` trigger, the `Send survey invite via email and wait for response` action, and the `survey_responses` and `response_answers` data pipeline objects require this permission.
   
   ![Authorization grant](/assets/authorization_grant.mzHGoRrt.png)_Authorize Workato to access your SurveyMonkey account._
   

## Configure the pipeline

Complete the following steps to configure SurveyMonkey as your data pipeline source:

1. Select **Create > Data pipeline** or press C+I.
   
2. Enter a name for the data pipeline in the **Data pipeline name** field.
   
   ![Data pipeline setup](/assets/set-up-pipeline.Cxx6hIk2.png)_Data pipeline setup_
   
3. Use the **Location** drop-down menu to select the project where you plan to store the data pipeline.
   
4. Click **Start building**.
   
5. Click the **Extract new/updated records from source app** trigger. This trigger defines how the pipeline retrieves data from SurveyMonkey.
   
   ![Configure the Extract new/updated records from source app trigger](/assets/choose-source-app.B2OOUpgY.png)_Configure the Extract new/updated records from source app trigger_
   
6. Use the **Your Connected Source Apps** drop-down menu to select **SurveyMonkey**.
   
7. Choose the SurveyMonkey connection you plan to use for this pipeline. Alternatively, click **\+ New connection** to create a new connection.
   
8. Click **Add object** to open the **Add new objects** panel.
   
   ![Add objects](/assets/add-objects-surveymonkey.Dxy0DOXU.png)_Add objects_
   
9. Search or browse the list of available SurveyMonkey objects, select the objects you plan to sync, and click **Add**.
   
   > **FULL SYNC ONLY OBJECTS**
   > 
   > Objects without an incremental cursor, such as `survey_pages` and `response_answers`, are labeled **Full sync** in the object list and always sync in full. Refer to [Sync modes](#sync-modes) for more information.
   
10. Optional. Click the gear icon next to an object to open its sync mode settings. Use the **Sync mode** drop-down menu to select **Full sync** or **Incremental**, then click **Save**. Only `surveys`, `survey_responses`, and `collectors` support incremental sync.
    
11. Review and customize the schema for each selected object. The pipeline automatically fetches an object's schema when you select it. This ensures the destination matches the source.
    
    Expand an object to view associated fields. Keep all fields selected to extract all available data, or deselect specific fields to exclude them from data extraction and schema replication.
    
12. Optional. Configure field-level data protection by expanding an object and choosing how to handle each field:
    
    - **Replicate as is**: Data values at the source replicate identically to the destination.
    - **Hash**: Hash sensitive data values in the field before syncing to your destination.
    
    Workato recommends hashing personally identifiable information (PII) and other sensitive fields. Refer to [Sensitive data handling](#sensitive-data-handling) for a list of fields that commonly contain PII.
    
13. Click **Add object** again to add more objects. Repeat this step to include additional SurveyMonkey objects in your pipeline.
    
14. Use the **Choose how to handle schema changes** drop-down menu to select a schema drift handling option:
    
    - **Auto-sync new fields**: Automatically detects and syncs new fields added in the source.
    - **Block new fields**: Keeps the schema fixed after the pipeline starts. You must add new fields manually. This option may cause the destination to fall out of sync if the source schema updates.
    
    Refer to [Schema replication and schema drift management](/en/data-orchestration/data-pipeline-recipe/concepts#schema-drift) for more information.
    
15. Optional. Enter a value in the **Concurrency limit** field to cap the number of concurrent operations. Leave the field blank to use the default limit set by Workato. The maximum value is `100`.
    
16. Choose either a standard time-based schedule or define a custom cron expression in the **Frequency** field. This determines how often the pipeline syncs data from SurveyMonkey to the destination.
    
    **Time-based schedule**
    
    1. Select the **Time unit**, such as **Minutes**, **Hours**, or **Days**.
       
    2. Specify the sync interval in the **Trigger every** field.
       
       For example, the pipeline syncs every 6 hours if you select **Hours** as the **Time unit** and enter `6` in the **Trigger every** field.
       
       The minimum interval you can set is 15 minutes.
       
    3. Select a start date for the historical data sync in the **When first started, this pipeline should pick up records from** field. This defines the earliest date from which the pipeline extracts records. The pipeline picks up all available records from the source if you leave this field blank.
       
       You can't change this value after you run the pipeline.
       
    4. Click **Save** to save your progress before you [configure your data pipeline destination](/en/data-orchestration/data-pipeline-recipe/configure-pipeline-destinations#configure‒how‒data‒is‒loaded‒in‒the‒workato‒data‒pipeline).
       
    
    **Cron-based scheduling**
    
    1. Use the **Time unit** drop-down menu to select **Custom schedule**.
       
    2. Enter an expression in the **Cron expression** field using the format:
       
       ```text
       [minute] [hour] [day of month] [month] [day of week]
       ```
       
       The minimum interval for cron schedules is 15 minutes.
       
       For example, enter the following expression to sync every day at 8:00 AM UTC:
       
       ```text
       0 8 * * *
       ```
       
    3. Optional. Select a **Timezone** for the cron expression. Leave blank to use `Etc/UTC`.
       
    4. Select a start date for the historical data sync in the **When first started, this pipeline should pick up records from** field. This defines the earliest date from which the pipeline extracts records. The pipeline picks up all available records from the source if you leave this field blank.
       
       You can't change this value after you run the pipeline.
       
    5. Click **Save** to save your progress before you [configure your data pipeline destination](/en/data-orchestration/data-pipeline-recipe/configure-pipeline-destinations#configure‒how‒data‒is‒loaded‒in‒the‒workato‒data‒pipeline).
       
    
    SurveyMonkey objects apply the start date differently. Refer to [The start date applies differently by object](#the-start-date-applies-differently-by-object) for more information.
    

## Supported objects

SurveyMonkey data pipelines sync data from the SurveyMonkey REST API v3. The following tables list the supported objects, grouped by category. Each object syncs as a separate table in your destination.

### Surveys and survey structure

| Object | Sync mode(s) | Delete tracking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `surveys` | Full sync, incremental | No |
| `survey_pages` | Full sync | Yes |
| `survey_questions` | Full sync | Yes |
| `question_options` | Full sync | Yes |
| `question_sub_rows` | Full sync | Yes |

`survey_pages`, `survey_questions`, `question_options`, and `question_sub_rows` store each survey's structure. `question_options` contains the answer choices for each question, and `question_sub_rows` contains the rows of matrix and other multi-row questions.

### Responses

`survey_responses` and `response_answers` require a paid SurveyMonkey plan. Refer to [Responses require a paid plan](#responses-require-a-paid-plan) for more information.

| Object | Sync mode(s) | Delete tracking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `survey_responses` | Full sync, incremental | No |
| `response_answers` | Full sync | Yes |

`response_answers` contains one row per answer in each response. Join `response_answers` to `question_options` on `question_id` and `choice_id` (matched to `question_options.id`) to resolve a selected answer to its choice text.

### Collectors

| Object | Sync mode(s) | Delete tracking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `collectors` | Full sync, incremental | No |
| `collector_recipients` | Full sync | Yes |

`collector_recipients` contains recipients of email and SMS collectors only. Other collector types, such as web links and embedded surveys, have no recipient list.

## Sync modes

SurveyMonkey data pipelines support full sync and incremental sync. You configure the sync mode per object when you add it to your pipeline.

### Full sync

A full sync reads all available records from SurveyMonkey for the selected object. Survey structure objects, `response_answers` and `collector_recipients`, use full sync because SurveyMonkey doesn't expose a last-modified timestamp for them.

Every SurveyMonkey object has a primary key, so a full sync merges into the existing destination table, and records deleted in SurveyMonkey stay in the table.

### Incremental sync

An incremental sync extracts only records that changed since the last successful run, using the `date_modified` field as the cursor:

- **`surveys`**: Extracts surveys modified since the last run.
- **`survey_responses`**: Tracks a separate cursor for each survey and checks every survey on each run, so new and edited responses sync even when the parent survey hasn't changed.
- **`collectors`**: Extracts collectors modified since the last run.

Each incremental run rereads the last `5` minutes of the previous window to capture records modified at the window boundary. Your destination's upsert behavior deduplicates rereads by primary key.

### Delete tracking

SurveyMonkey's API doesn't report deleted surveys, responses, or collectors. Workato tracks deletions in the following ways:

- **Full-sync objects**: Workato marks records that no longer appear in SurveyMonkey as deleted in your destination. Deletions are detected on the next full sync, not at the time of deletion.
- **`survey_questions`**: SurveyMonkey keeps deleted questions in the API and sets their `visible` field to `false`. Workato sets `_workato_is_deleted` to `true` for these questions.
- **Incremental objects**: Deletions aren't detected for `surveys`, `survey_responses`, or `collectors`. An incremental run only pulls changed records, so deleted records remain in your destination.

## Schema and data type handling

The following considerations apply to schema and data types when you sync data from SurveyMonkey:

### Nested fields

Nested and variable-shape fields sync as JSON objects stored in your destination's native JSON type, such as `VARIANT` in Snowflake. These fields include `headings`, `answers`, and `validation` on `survey_questions`, and `metadata`, `logic_path`, `page_path`, and `custom_variables` on `survey_responses`. Workato doesn't flatten these into individual columns. `custom_variables` keys vary by survey.

### Timestamps

SurveyMonkey returns survey timestamps without a time zone offset and response and collector timestamps with an offset. Workato syncs `date_created` and `date_modified` on `surveys` as timestamps without a time zone, in UTC. The same fields on `survey_responses` and `collectors` sync as timestamps with a time zone.

### Response answer keys

`response_answers` uses a composite primary key of `response_id`, `question_id`, `row_id`, `col_id`, `choice_id`, and `other_id`. Key columns that don't apply to a question type contain an empty string, not `null`. For example, `row_id` and `col_id` are empty for single-choice questions.

### Collector recipient custom fields

`collector_recipients` includes six custom field columns, `custom_field_1` through `custom_field_6`, that map to the first six contact custom fields in your SurveyMonkey account. Workato labels these columns with your account's custom field labels when the connection grants the `contacts_read` scope.

### Synthetic columns

Workato adds the following synthetic column to the `survey_questions` destination table:

| Column | Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `_workato_is_deleted` | Boolean | Set to `true` when SurveyMonkey marks the question as deleted (`visible` is `false`). |

## Sensitive data handling

SurveyMonkey objects can contain personally identifiable information (PII). The following objects commonly contain sensitive fields:

| Object | Sensitive fields |
| --- | --- |
| `survey_responses` | `first_name`, `last_name`, `email_address`, `ip_address`, `custom_value`, `custom_variables`, `metadata` |
| `response_answers` | `text` |
| `collectors` | `email` |
| `collector_recipients` | `email`, `phone_number`, `custom_field_1` through `custom_field_6` |

`response_answers.text` contains free-text answers to open-ended questions, which can include names, contact details, and other personal information. `custom_variables` can contain any values you pass to a survey, and `metadata` includes the respondent's referral URL and user agent.

Use the **Hash** option in field-level data protection during pipeline configuration to protect PII before it reaches your destination. Refer to the [Configure the pipeline](#configure-the-pipeline) steps for more information.

## Limitations

The following limitations apply when you use SurveyMonkey as a data pipeline source:

### Responses require a paid plan

SurveyMonkey provides response details only to accounts on a paid plan. Syncs of `survey_responses` and `response_answers` fail on a free plan account. Remove these objects from your pipeline or upgrade your SurveyMonkey plan.

### The start date applies differently by object

The **When first started, this pipeline should pick up records from** date filters SurveyMonkey objects in the following ways:

- **Survey objects**: `surveys`, `survey_pages`, `survey_questions`, `question_options`, and `question_sub_rows` include only surveys modified after this date. Survey structure objects exclude older surveys even if those surveys still receive responses.
- **Responses and collectors**: `survey_responses` and `collectors` apply this date to each record's `date_modified` value on the first incremental sync. A full sync of these objects ignores the start date and extracts all records.
- **Answers and recipients**: `response_answers` and `collector_recipients` ignore the start date and extract all records on every run.

Leave this field blank to sync the structure of every survey.

### Surveys with more than 1,000 questions

SurveyMonkey doesn't return the structure of surveys with more than `1,000` questions. Workato skips the survey structure objects for these surveys and continues the sync. The `surveys` record for the survey still syncs.

### Preview responses aren't synced

`survey_responses` and `response_answers` exclude test responses submitted from a collector preview link or the survey builder's preview. All other responses sync, including manually entered and edited responses.

### Collector recipient data

`collector_recipients` doesn't include recipient first and last names, because SurveyMonkey doesn't return them in the recipient list. Custom field values sync only for the first `6` contact custom fields in your account.

### Minimum sync frequency

The minimum supported sync interval is `15` minutes.

# Configure Trello as a data pipeline source

Set up Trello as a data pipeline source to extract boards, cards, and related project data into your destination.

Use this guide to create a connection, configure your pipeline, add objects, review sync behavior, and understand known limitations.

## Trello features supported

The following features are supported when you use Trello as a pipeline source:

- **Sign-in authentication**: Connect by signing in to your Trello account and authorizing Workato's access. Refer to [Supported connection types](#supported-connection-types) for more information.
- **Full sync and incremental sync**: Board and card structure objects use full sync on every run. Board and organization activity objects use incremental sync based on a creation-time cursor. Refer to [Sync modes](#sync-modes) for more information.
- **Delete tracking**: Detect deletions for full-sync objects by comparing successive syncs. Refer to [Delete tracking](#delete-tracking) for more information.
- **Object-level selection**: Choose which Trello objects to sync into your destination.
- **Schema drift detection and handling**: Detect and apply schema changes automatically with **Auto-sync new fields**, or keep the schema fixed with **Block new fields**.
- **Field-level data protection**: Hash or replicate sensitive fields as is before the data reaches your destination.
- **Configurable sync frequency**: Schedule syncs on a time-based interval or with a cron expression. The minimum supported interval is 15 minutes.

## Trello prerequisites

Connecting Trello as a data pipeline source requires:

- A Trello account that's a member of every board you plan to sync. The connected account can only view boards it belongs to, because Trello doesn't expose a workspace-wide listing endpoint. Refer to [Membership-scoped extraction](#membership-scoped-extraction) for more information.
- Permission to sign in and authorize Workato's access to that account.

> **ACCESS REQUESTED DURING SIGN-IN**
> 
> Workato requests read access to your boards, cards, and organizations, plus access to your own account details. Trello may return `Member.email` only for the account that authorized the connection. The field can be empty for other members and may be unavailable when Trello restricts email access. Refer to [Member email is restricted](#member-email-is-restricted) for more information.

## Supported connection types

Trello data pipelines connect by signing in to your Trello account and authorizing Workato's access. This grants Workato an access token scoped to your account. Workato pairs this token with a Trello API key for extraction requests, using its own registered key by default or a key from a linked Custom OAuth profile if you use one. Refer to [Connect to Trello](#connect-to-trello) for setup steps.

## Connect to Trello

Connect to Trello

Complete the following steps to connect to Trello in Workato:

1. Click **Create > Connection** or press C twice.
   
2. Search for `Trello` and select it as your app.
   
3. Enter a name for your connection in the **Connection name** field.
   
   ![Connect to Trello](/assets/connect-to-trello.thFd_ZNH.png)_Connect to Trello_
   
4. Use the **Location** drop-down menu to select the project where you plan to store the connection.
   
5. Optional. Use the **Custom OAuth profile** drop-down menu to select a custom OAuth profile for your connection.
   
6. Click **Connect**.
   
7. Sign in to the Trello account you plan to connect to, then click **Allow** to grant Workato access and complete the connection.
   

## Configure the pipeline

Complete the following steps to configure Trello as your data pipeline source:

1. Select **Create > Data pipeline**.
   
2. Enter a name for the data pipeline in the **Data pipeline name** field.
   
   ![Data pipeline setup](/assets/set-up-pipeline.Cxx6hIk2.png)_Data pipeline setup_
   
3. Use the **Location** drop-down menu to select the project where you plan to store the data pipeline.
   
4. Click **Start building**.
   
5. Click the **Extract new/updated records from source app** trigger. This trigger defines how the pipeline retrieves data from Trello.
   
   ![Configure the Extract new/updated records from source app trigger](/assets/choose-source-app.B2OOUpgY.png)_Configure the Extract new/updated records from source app trigger_
   
6. Use the **Your Connected Source Apps** drop-down menu to select **Trello**.
   
7. Choose the Trello connection you plan to use for this pipeline. Alternatively, click **\+ New connection** to create a new connection.
   
8. Click **Add object** to open the **Add new objects** panel.
   
   ![Add objects](/assets/add-objects-trello.C3F_MFmY.png)_Add objects_
   
9. Search or browse the list of available Trello objects, select the objects you plan to sync, and click **Add**.
   
   > **INCREMENTAL SYNC AVAILABILITY**
   > 
   > Only the `Action` and `OrganizationAction` objects support incremental sync. Every other Trello object syncs through full sync only. Refer to [Sync modes](#sync-modes) for more information.
   
10. Optional. Click the gear icon next to an object to open its **Sync mode** settings. Use the **Sync mode** drop-down menu to select **Full sync** or **Incremental**, then click **Save**.
    
    The sync mode defaults to **Full sync** for objects that don't support incremental sync, including objects without a usable cursor and child objects that sync with a parent. Refer to [Sync modes](#sync-modes) for more information.
    
11. Review and customize the schema for each selected object. The pipeline automatically fetches an object's schema when you select it, so the destination matches the source.
    
    Expand an object to view associated fields. Keep all fields selected to extract all available data, or deselect specific fields to exclude them from data extraction and schema replication.
    
12. Optional. Configure field-level data protection by expanding an object and choosing how to handle each field:
    
    - **Replicate as is**: Data values at the source replicate identically to the destination.
    - **Hash**: Hash sensitive data values in the field before syncing to your destination.
    
    Workato recommends hashing personally identifiable information (PII) and other sensitive fields. Refer to [Sensitive data handling](#sensitive-data-handling) for a list of fields that commonly contain PII.
    
13. Click **Add object** again to add more objects. Repeat the preceding steps for each additional object to configure its sync mode, schema, and field-level data protection.
    
14. Use the **Choose how to handle schema changes** drop-down menu to select a schema drift handling option:
    
    - **Auto-sync new fields**: Automatically detects and syncs new fields added in the source.
    - **Block new fields**: Keeps the schema fixed after the pipeline starts. You must add new fields manually.
15. Optional. Enter a value in the **Concurrency limit** field to cap the number of concurrent operations. Leave the field blank to use the default quota set by Workato. The maximum value is `100`.
    
16. Configure how often the pipeline syncs data from Trello to the destination in the **Frequency** field. Choose either a standard time-based schedule or define a custom cron expression.
    
    **Time-based schedule**
    
    1. Select the **Time unit**, such as **Minutes**, **Hours**, or **Days**.
       
    2. Specify the sync interval in the **Trigger every** field.
       
       For example, if you select **Hours** as the **Time unit** and enter **6** in the **Trigger every** field, the pipeline syncs every 6 hours. The minimum interval you can set is 15 minutes.
       
    3. Select a start date for the historical data sync in the **When first started, this pipeline should pick up records from** field. This defines the earliest date from which the pipeline extracts records. The pipeline picks up all available records from the source if you leave this field blank.
       
       You can't change this value after you run the pipeline.
       
    4. Click **Save** to save your progress before you [configure your data pipeline destination](/en/data-orchestration/data-pipeline-recipe/configure-pipeline-destinations#configure‒how‒data‒is‒loaded‒in‒the‒workato‒data‒pipeline).
       
    
    **Cron-based scheduling**
    
    1. Use the **Time unit** drop-down menu to select **Custom schedule**.
       
    2. Enter an expression in the **Cron expression** field using the format:
       
       ```text
       [minute] [hour] [day of month] [month] [day of week]
       ```
       
       The minimum interval for cron schedules is 15 minutes. For example, enter the following expression to sync every day at 8:00 AM UTC:
       
       ```text
       0 8 * * *
       ```
       
    3. Optional. Select a **Timezone** for the cron expression. Leave blank to use `Etc/UTC`.
       
    4. Select a start date for the historical data sync in the **When first started, this pipeline should pick up records from** field. This defines the earliest date from which the pipeline extracts records. The pipeline picks up all available records from the source if you leave this field blank.
       
       You can't change this value after you run the pipeline.
       
    5. Click **Save** to save your progress before you [configure your data pipeline destination](/en/data-orchestration/data-pipeline-recipe/configure-pipeline-destinations#configure‒how‒data‒is‒loaded‒in‒the‒workato‒data‒pipeline).
       
    

## Supported Trello objects

Trello data pipelines sync data from the Trello REST API. The following tables list the supported objects, grouped by category. Each object syncs as a separate table in your destination.

### Boards and organizations

| Object | Sync modes | Delete tracking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Board` | Full sync | Yes |
| `Organization` | Full sync | Yes |

### Board structure

| Object | Sync modes | Delete tracking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `List` | Full sync | Yes |
| `Label` | Full sync | Yes |
| `Member` | Full sync | Yes |
| `Checklist` | Full sync | Yes |
| `CustomField` | Full sync | Yes |

### Cards

| Object | Sync modes | Delete tracking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Card` | Full sync | Yes |
| `CardMember` | Syncs with the parent `Card` object | Yes |
| `CardLabel` | Syncs with the parent `Card` object | Yes |
| `CheckItem` | Syncs with the parent `Checklist` object | Yes |
| `CustomFieldItem` | Syncs with the parent `Card` object | Yes |
| `CardAttachment` | Syncs with the parent `Card` object | Yes |

`CustomFieldItem` stores custom field values. Join it to `CustomField` on `idCustomField` to interpret each value. Refer to [Custom fields](#custom-fields) for more information.

`CardAttachment` contains attachment metadata only. Workato doesn't replicate attachment file contents. Refer to [Card attachments contain metadata only](#card-attachments-contain-metadata-only) for more information.

### Activity

| Object | Sync modes | Delete tracking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Action` | Full sync, incremental | No (Yes in full sync) |
| `OrganizationAction` | Full sync, incremental | No (Yes in full sync) |

`Action` contains board-, list-, and card-level activity, including card comments. `OrganizationAction` contains organization-level activity. Refer to [Comments live in the Action object](#comments-live-in-the-action-object) for more information.

### Organization structure

| Object | Sync modes | Delete tracking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OrganizationMember` | Syncs with the parent `Organization` object | Yes |
| `OrganizationTag` | Full sync | Yes |

## Sync modes

Trello data pipelines support full sync and incremental sync. The sync mode is configured per object when you add it to your pipeline.

### Full sync

A full sync reads all available records from Trello for the selected object on every run. Workato re-extracts board, card, and organization structure objects in full on every scheduled run to capture edits, moves, and archival changes, because Trello doesn't expose a reliable last-updated timestamp on these objects. Archived boards, lists, and cards remain included in a full sync and are distinguished from active records through the source `closed` field, not removed from the sync.

Objects with a primary key merge into the existing destination table, so records deleted in Trello stay in the table. Objects without a primary key overwrite the destination table on every run.

### Incremental sync

An incremental sync extracts only records created since the last successful run. The `Action` and `OrganizationAction` objects use a creation-time cursor on the source `date` field. Each run rereads the most recent `1` day of activity in addition to any new activity, so recently edited comments can be picked up again by the same record `id`. This overlap doesn't guarantee that every historical edit or deletion is captured. Refer to [Comments live in the Action object](#comments-live-in-the-action-object) for more information.

Refer to the [Supported objects](#supported-objects) tables to see which objects support incremental sync.

### Delete tracking

Workato compares each full sync against the previous run and marks records that no longer appear in Trello as deleted in your destination. This applies to every full-sync object, including `Action` and `OrganizationAction` when you run them in full sync mode.

`Action` and `OrganizationAction` don't track deletes while running incrementally, because incremental sync only reads new activity and doesn't capture a complete snapshot to compare against. Trello also doesn't provide a native delete signal on these objects. Most delete and remove event types aren't included in the activity feed at all. A record deleted in Trello stays in your destination for these objects.

Refer to the [Supported objects](#supported-objects) tables to see which objects support delete tracking.

## Schema and data type handling

The following considerations apply to schema and data types when you sync data from Trello.

### Custom fields

Trello board custom fields sync as two objects. `CustomField` holds each field's definition (name and type), and `CustomFieldItem` holds each card's value for that field in a generic `value` column. Workato doesn't flatten custom field values into individual typed columns, because dropdown values are ID-referenced and the field set can differ per board. Join `CustomFieldItem.idCustomField` to `CustomField.id` to interpret a value.

`CustomField` and `CustomFieldItem` return no rows for a board rather than an error if the Custom Fields Power-Up isn't enabled on that board.

### JSON fields

Trello returns several fields as nested objects or arrays, such as `Card.badges`, `Card.idMembers`, `Board.prefs`, and `Action.data`. Workato preserves these as JSON columns in your destination rather than flattening them.

### Position values

The `pos` field on `List`, `Card`, `CardAttachment`, and other ordered objects is a decimal number, not a sequential integer. Don't assume a fixed or gap-free sequence, because Trello reassigns `pos` values when a customer reorders items.

## Sensitive data handling

Trello objects can contain personally identifiable information (PII) in free-text fields. The following objects commonly contain sensitive fields:

| Object | Sensitive fields |
| --- | --- |
| `Card` | `desc`, `name`, `email`, `sourceEmail`, `address`, `locationName`, `coordinates` |
| `Member` | `fullName`, `username`, `avatarUrl`, `bio`, `email` |
| `Action` | `data` (includes comment text for `commentCard` events) |
| `CardAttachment` | `name`, `url` |
| `CustomFieldItem` | `value` |
| `Organization` | `name`, `displayName`, `desc`, `website` |

Customers can paste any PII into `Card.desc` and comment text in `Action.data`, because these fields are free text. `Member.email` may populate only for the account that authorized the connection. Refer to [Member email is restricted](#member-email-is-restricted) for more information.

Use the **Hash** option in field-level data protection during pipeline configuration to protect PII before it reaches your destination. Refer to the [Configure the pipeline](#configure-the-pipeline) steps for more information.

## Trello limitations

The following limitations apply when you use Trello as a data pipeline source:

### Membership-scoped extraction

This connector discovers boards through the connected member's membership-scoped board list, and organizations the same way. Boards that the connected user cannot access, along with their cards, lists, and other child objects, aren't extracted, with no error raised. Add the connected account to every board you want to sync, or use a dedicated Trello account added to all relevant boards.

### Member email is restricted

Trello may return `Member.email` only for the account that authorized the Workato connection. The field can be empty for other members, regardless of that member's role or permissions, and may be unavailable when Trello restricts email access.

### Card attachments contain metadata only

The `CardAttachment` object syncs file and link metadata, such as `name`, `url`, and `mimeType`. Workato doesn't replicate attachment file contents. Uploaded-file URLs require the original Trello session to access and may not resolve outside it.

### Comments live in the Action object

Trello card comments aren't a separate object. They sync as `commentCard` rows in the `Action` object, with the comment text in the `data` field. An edit is only picked up again if it falls inside the incremental sync's `1`\-day lookback window, because editing a comment doesn't change its `Action` `id` or `date`. Deleting a comment removes it from Trello's activity feed entirely, with no corresponding record in `Action` to signal the deletion.

### Minimum sync frequency

The minimum supported sync interval is 15 minutes.

# Configure Typeform as a data pipeline source

Set up Typeform as a data pipeline source to extract and sync forms, responses, and account resources such as workspaces, themes, webhooks, and images from Typeform to your destination.

Use this guide to review the features and prerequisites, connect Typeform as a data pipeline source, configure the pipeline, and understand the supported objects, sync modes, schema handling, sensitive data handling, and known limitations.

## Typeform features supported

The following features are supported when you use Typeform as a pipeline source:

- **Cloud connectivity**: Connects to the Typeform API over HTTPS. An on-prem agent isn't required.
- **Data center selection**: Connect to an account that stores responses in the US data center or the EU data center. Refer to [Supported data centers](#supported-data-centers) for more information.
- **Object-level selection**: Choose from `Forms`, `Responses`, `Response Answers`, and account resources. Refer to [Supported objects](#supported-objects) for the full list.
- **Incremental sync**: Response objects sync incrementally based on each response's `submitted_at` or `staged_at` timestamp. Refer to [Incremental sync](#incremental-sync) for more information.
- **Partial and completed responses**: Response objects include partial and completed responses. Refer to [Partial responses](#partial-responses) for more information.
- **Delete tracking**: Mark records you delete in Typeform as deleted in your destination on the next full sync. Refer to [Delete tracking](#delete-tracking) for more information.
- **Schema drift detection and handling**: Detect and apply schema changes automatically with **Auto-sync new fields**, or keep the schema fixed with **Block new fields**.
- **Field-level data protection**: Hash or replicate sensitive fields as is before the data reaches your destination.
- **Configurable sync frequency**: Schedule syncs on a time-based interval or with a cron expression. The minimum supported interval is 15 minutes.

## Typeform prerequisites

Connecting Typeform as a data pipeline source requires:

- A Typeform account with access to the forms you plan to sync.
- A Typeform application and a [custom OAuth profile](/en/custom-oauth-profiles) built from that application's client ID and client secret. Refer to [Create a Typeform OAuth app and custom OAuth profile](#create-a-typeform-oauth-app-and-custom-oauth-profile) for setup steps.

## Supported connection types

Typeform data pipelines support OAuth 2.0 authentication:

- **OAuth 2.0**: Authorize Workato using a custom OAuth profile built from a Typeform application that you create. Refer to [Create a Typeform OAuth app and custom OAuth profile](#create-a-typeform-oauth-app-and-custom-oauth-profile) for setup steps. Personal access token authentication isn't supported.

## Connect to Typeform

Connect to Typeform

- [Create a Typeform OAuth app and custom OAuth profile](#create-a-typeform-oauth-app-and-custom-oauth-profile) to store your Typeform application's client ID and client secret in Workato.
- [Connect to Typeform with OAuth 2.0](#connect-to-typeform-with-oauth-2-0) using the custom OAuth profile you created.

### Create a Typeform OAuth app and custom OAuth profile

You must create a Typeform application and a Workato custom OAuth profile before you connect Typeform as a data pipeline source:

1. Go to **Tools > Custom OAuth profiles** in Workato and click **\+ New custom profile**.
   
2. Use the **Application** drop-down menu to select **Typeform**.
   
3. Enter a name in the **Name** field. The name can contain spaces but no special characters, and it must be unique for your account.
   
4. Click **Create new app**. Keep the Workato tab open.
   
5. Sign in to Typeform in a new tab and create an application using `https://www.workato.com/oauth/callback` as the redirect URI. Refer to the Typeform [Create an application](https://www.typeform.com/developers/get-started/applications/#1-create-an-application-in-the-typeform-admin-panel) guide for steps.
   
6. Copy the application's client ID and client secret and store them securely.
   
7. Return to the Workato tab and enter the values in the **Client ID** and **Client secret** fields.
   
8. Click **Save**. Refer to [Custom OAuth profiles](/en/custom-oauth-profiles) for more information.
   

### Connect to Typeform with OAuth 2.0

Complete the following steps to create a Typeform connection that uses your custom OAuth profile:

1. Select **Create > Connection** or press C twice.
   
2. Search for `Typeform` and select it as your app.
   
3. Enter a name in the **Connection name** field.
   
4. Use the **Location** drop-down menu to select the project where you plan to store the connection.
   
5. Use the **Data center** drop-down menu to select the data center where your Typeform account stores responses. Select **EU** if the EU Responses Data Center is enabled for your account. Otherwise, select **US**. The connection uses **US** if you leave this field blank. Refer to [Supported data centers](#supported-data-centers) for more information.
   
6. Use the **Custom OAuth profile** drop-down menu to select the [custom OAuth profile](#create-a-typeform-oauth-app-and-custom-oauth-profile) you created for Typeform. This field is required.
   
7. Click **Connect**.
   
8. Log in to your Typeform account in the window that opens to complete the connection. Workato displays a success message when the connection is established.
   

## Configure the pipeline

Complete the following steps to configure Typeform as your data pipeline source:

1. Select **Create > Data pipeline** or press C+I.
   
2. Enter a name for the data pipeline in the **Data pipeline name** field.
   
   ![Data pipeline setup](/assets/set-up-pipeline.Cxx6hIk2.png)_Data pipeline setup_
   
3. Use the **Location** drop-down menu to select the project where you plan to store the data pipeline.
   
4. Click **Start building**.
   
5. Click the **Extract new/updated records from source app** trigger. This trigger defines how the pipeline retrieves data from Typeform.
   
   ![Configure the Extract new/updated records from source app trigger](/assets/choose-source-app.B2OOUpgY.png)_Configure the Extract new/updated records from source app trigger_
   
6. Use the **Your Connected Source Apps** drop-down menu to select **Typeform**.
   
7. Choose the Typeform connection you plan to use for this pipeline. Alternatively, click **\+ New connection** to create a new connection.
   
8. Click **Add object** to open the **Add new objects** panel.
   
   ![Add objects](/assets/add-objects-typeform.B4Ut6BGV.png)_Add objects_
   
9. Search or browse the list of available Typeform objects, select the objects you plan to sync, and click **Add**.
   
10. Review and customize the schema for each selected object. The pipeline automatically fetches an object's schema when you select it. This ensures the destination matches the source.
    
    Expand an object to view associated fields. Keep all fields selected to extract all available data, or deselect specific fields to exclude them from data extraction and schema replication.
    
11. Optional. Configure field-level data protection by expanding an object and choosing how to handle each field:
    
    - **Replicate as is**: Data values at the source replicate identically to the destination.
    - **Hash**: Hash sensitive data values in the field before syncing to your destination.
    
    Workato recommends hashing personally identifiable information (PII) and other sensitive fields. Refer to [Sensitive data handling](#sensitive-data-handling) for a list of fields that commonly contain PII.
    
12. Click **Add object** again to add more objects. Repeat this step to include additional Typeform objects in your pipeline.
    
13. Use the **Choose how to handle schema changes** drop-down menu to select a schema drift handling option:
    
    - **Auto-sync new fields**: Automatically detects and syncs new fields added in the source.
    - **Block new fields**: Keeps the schema fixed after the pipeline starts. You must add new fields manually. This option may cause the destination to fall out of sync if the source schema updates.
    
    Refer to [Schema replication and schema drift management](/en/data-orchestration/data-pipeline-recipe/concepts#schema-drift) for more information.
    
14. Optional. Enter a value in the **Concurrency limit** field to cap the number of concurrent operations. Leave the field blank to use the default limit set by Workato. The maximum value for Typeform is `1`.
    
15. Choose either a standard time-based schedule or define a custom cron expression in the **Frequency** field. This determines how often the pipeline syncs data from Typeform to the destination.
    
    **Time-based schedule**
    
    1. Select the **Time unit**, such as **Minutes**, **Hours**, or **Days**.
       
    2. Specify the sync interval in the **Trigger every** field.
       
       The pipeline syncs every 6 hours, for example, if you select **Hours** as the **Time unit** and enter `6` in the **Trigger every** field. The minimum interval you can set is `15` minutes.
       
    3. Select a start date for the historical data sync in the **When first started, this pipeline should pick up records from** field. This defines the earliest date from which the pipeline extracts response objects. The pipeline picks up all available responses if you leave this field blank. `Forms`, `Workspaces`, `Themes`, `Webhooks`, and `Images` always sync in full and ignore this field.
       
       You can't change this value after you run the pipeline.
       
    4. Click **Save** to save your progress before you [configure your data pipeline destination](/en/data-orchestration/data-pipeline-recipe/configure-pipeline-destinations#configure‒how‒data‒is‒loaded‒in‒the‒workato‒data‒pipeline).
       
    
    **Cron-based scheduling**
    
    1. Use the **Time unit** drop-down menu to select **Custom schedule**.
       
    2. Enter an expression in the **Cron expression** field using the format:
       
       ```text
       [minute] [hour] [day of month] [month] [day of week]
       ```
       
       The minimum interval for cron schedules is `15` minutes. For example, enter the following expression to sync every day at 8:00 AM UTC:
       
       ```text
       0 8 * * *
       ```
       
    3. Optional. Select a **Timezone** for the cron expression. Leave blank to use `Etc/UTC`.
       
    4. Select a start date for the historical data sync in the **When first started, this pipeline should pick up records from** field. This defines the earliest date from which the pipeline extracts response objects. The pipeline picks up all available responses if you leave this field blank. `Forms`, `Workspaces`, `Themes`, `Webhooks`, and `Images` always sync in full and ignore this field.
       
       You can't change this value after you run the pipeline.
       
    5. Click **Save** to save your progress before you [configure your data pipeline destination](/en/data-orchestration/data-pipeline-recipe/configure-pipeline-destinations#configure‒how‒data‒is‒loaded‒in‒the‒workato‒data‒pipeline).
       
    

## Supported Typeform objects

Typeform data pipelines sync data from the Typeform Create, Responses, and Webhooks APIs. The following tables list the supported objects, grouped by category. Each object syncs as a separate table in your destination:

### Response objects

`Responses` contains one row for each form response. `Response Answers` contains one row for each answer. `Response Answer Choices` contains one row for each selected choice. `Response Variables` contains one row for each variable or hidden field. Workato reads all four objects from the responses of every form in your account, so you can select each one independently.

| Object | Sync mode(s) | Delete tracking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Responses` | Full sync, incremental | No |
| `Response Answers` | Full sync, incremental | No |
| `Response Answer Choices` | Full sync, incremental | No |
| `Response Variables` | Full sync, incremental | No |

### Form and account objects

The following objects sync forms and the resources in your Typeform account. `Forms` contains summary fields only. Refer to [Form definitions aren't synced](#form-definitions-arent-synced) for more information. `Webhooks` contains the webhooks configured on each form, without the webhook secret. `Images` contains image metadata, such as the file name, URL, and dimensions, and doesn't download image files.

| Object | Sync mode(s) | Delete tracking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Forms` | Full sync | Yes |
| `Workspaces` | Full sync | Yes |
| `Themes` | Full sync | Yes |
| `Webhooks` | Full sync | Yes |
| `Images` | Full sync | Yes |

## Sync modes

Typeform data pipelines support full sync and incremental sync. Refer to the [Supported objects](#supported-objects) tables to see the sync modes for each object.

### Full sync

A full sync reads all records for the selected object from Typeform on every run. `Forms`, `Workspaces`, `Themes`, `Webhooks`, and `Images` support full sync only, because the Typeform API doesn't offer a way to request only changed records for these objects.

Objects with a primary key merge into the existing destination table, so records deleted in Typeform stay in the table. Objects without a primary key overwrite the destination table on every run.

Response objects also support full sync, which reads every response from the start date you configure.

### Incremental sync

Response objects filter responses by the `submitted_at` timestamp for completed responses and the `staged_at` timestamp for partial responses. The `cursor_at` column contains the timestamp used for each row.

Each incremental sync reads responses from `60` minutes before the previous successful sync started, because Typeform can take up to about `30` minutes to make new responses available. Your destination deduplicates re-read rows by primary key, so they update existing rows instead of creating duplicates.

### Partial responses

Response objects include partial responses alongside completed responses. A partial response contains the answers a respondent submitted before leaving the form. The `response_type` column contains `partial` or `completed`. Responses with the `started` type aren't synced.

Typeform records partial responses only on plans that support the partial responses feature.

### Delete tracking

Delete tracking depends on the object:

- **Full-sync objects**: `Yes`. Workato marks records you delete in Typeform as deleted in your destination on the next full sync.
- **Response objects**: `No`. The Typeform API doesn't expose deleted responses.

Answers, choices, and variables can also disappear from a partial response when the respondent edits it. Incremental syncs don't remove these rows, so they remain in `Response Answers`, `Response Answer Choices`, and `Response Variables`. Run a [full re-sync](/en/data-orchestration/sync-types#full-re-sync) to rebuild these tables. A full re-sync reloads every object in the pipeline.

## Schema and data type handling

The following considerations apply to schema and data types when you sync data from Typeform:

### Fixed schema

Every object has a fixed schema defined by Workato. New questions and hidden fields that you add to a form appear as new rows in `Response Answers` and `Response Variables`, not as new columns.

### Answer values

`Response Answers` stores each answer value in the column that matches its type, such as `text`, `email`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `phone_number`, `url`, `file_url`, `choice_label`, or `choices_labels`. The `answer_type` column identifies the populated column. Answers with a type that doesn't have its own column sync to the `raw_answer` column.

File upload answers sync the file URL that Typeform returns in `file_url`. Workato doesn't download the file, and Typeform file URLs expire.

### Variables and hidden fields

`Response Variables` contains one row for each variable and each hidden field on a response. The `value_source` column contains `variable` or `hidden`, which keeps a variable and a hidden field with the same key in separate rows. Text values sync to `text_value`, numeric values sync to `number_value`, and other values sync to `raw_value`.

### Timestamps

Timestamp fields, such as `created_at`, `submitted_at`, `staged_at`, and `cursor_at`, sync as ISO 8601 strings in UTC.

### Nested fields

Nested objects and arrays, such as `metadata`, `hidden`, and `calculated` on `Responses`, `colors` and `screens` on `Themes`, and `event_types` on `Webhooks`, sync as JSON objects. Workato stores them in your destination's native JSON type, such as `VARIANT` in Snowflake, and serializes them to strings only when the destination doesn't have a native JSON type.

### Synthetic columns

Workato adds the following columns to destination tables for specific objects:

| Column | Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `form_id` | String | ID of the form that the row belongs to. Added to `Responses`, `Response Answers`, `Response Answer Choices`, `Response Variables`, and `Webhooks`. Part of the primary key on `Response Answers`, `Response Answer Choices`, `Response Variables`, and `Webhooks`. |
| `cursor_at` | String | Added to response objects. Contains `submitted_at` for completed responses and `staged_at` for partial responses. |
| `choice_index` | Integer | Part of the `Response Answer Choices` primary key. Zero-based position of the choice in the answer. The **Other** free-text value syncs as the last choice, in the `other_text` column. |
| `value_source` | String | Part of the `Response Variables` primary key. Contains `variable` or `hidden`. |

## Sensitive data handling

Typeform responses often contain personally identifiable information (PII), because respondents can enter any information a form asks for. Treat free-text answers as sensitive, not only fields with obvious names such as `email`. The following objects commonly contain sensitive fields:

| Object | Sensitive fields |
| --- | --- |
| `Responses` | `hidden`, `metadata` (includes the IP-derived `network_id`, `browser`, `platform`, and `referer`) |
| `Response Answers` | `text`, `email`, `phone_number`, `url`, `file_url`, `raw_answer` |
| `Response Answer Choices` | `other_text` |
| `Response Variables` | `text_value`, `raw_value` |
| `Webhooks` | `url` |

Hidden fields often carry a respondent's email address or customer ID.

Use the **Hash** option in field-level data protection during pipeline configuration to protect PII before it reaches your destination. Refer to the [Configure the pipeline](#configure-the-pipeline) steps for more information.

## Typeform limitations

The following limitations apply when you use Typeform as a data pipeline source:

### Supported data centers

Typeform data pipelines support the US data center at `api.typeform.com` and the EU data center at `api.eu.typeform.com`. Accounts hosted in Typeform's newer EU data center at `api.typeform.eu` aren't supported.

Response objects fail with an error if the **Data center** you select doesn't match the data center where your account stores responses. Change the **Data center** setting to match your account, then reconnect to resolve the error.

### Form definitions aren't synced

`Forms` syncs the summary fields that Typeform returns when it lists forms, such as the title, type, timestamps, visibility, and links. Question definitions, logic jumps, and hidden field declarations aren't synced. Use `field_id`, `field_ref`, and `field_type` in `Response Answers` to identify the question each answer belongs to.

### Webhooks limit per form

`Webhooks` fails with an error if a single form has more than 1,000 webhooks.

### Minimum sync frequency

The minimum supported sync interval is 15 minutes.

# Configure Workday as a data pipeline source

Set up Workday as a data pipeline source to extract business object records from your Workday tenant and sync to your destination. Use this guide to set up a connection, configure your pipeline, add objects, review sync behavior, and understand known limitations.

## Workday features supported

The following features are supported when you use Workday as a pipeline source:

| Feature | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Authentication | Supports OAuth 2.0 and basic authentication. OAuth 2.0 is required to work with custom objects and Workday Query Language (WQL). Refer to [Supported connection types](#supported-connection-types) for more information. |
| Object selection | Select individual Workday business objects to sync as objects in your pipeline. Refer to [Supported objects](#supported-objects) for more information. |
| Field-level data protection | Configure each field to replicate values as-is or hash sensitive values before syncing to the destination. Refer to [Configure the pipeline](#configure-the-pipeline) for more information. |
| Schema drift detection and handling | Detect and apply schema changes automatically with **Auto-sync new fields**, or keep the schema fixed with **Block new fields**. |
| Configurable sync frequency | Schedule syncs on a time-based interval or with a custom cron expression. The minimum supported interval is 15 minutes. |
| Full refresh and incremental sync | Supports full refresh and incremental sync modes. Refer to [Sync modes](#sync-modes) for more information. |
| Delete tracking | Captures record deletions from Workday through a `Workato Is Deleted` flag on each record. Refer to [Schema and data type handling](#schema-and-data-type-handling) for more information. |

## Workday prerequisites

Complete the following requirements before you connect Workday as a data pipeline source.

- A Workday tenant you can administer, or admin access.
- An Integration System User (ISU) configured in Workday with the permissions required to read the business objects you plan to sync. Refer to [Register an Integration System User (ISU) in Workday](/en/connectors/workday#connection-setup) in the Workday connector documentation for setup steps.
- A registered API client for integrations in Workday with a non-expiring refresh token, and the client ID, client secret, authorization endpoint, and token endpoint values from the API client settings, if you plan to use OAuth 2.0.
- The ISU login name and password, if you plan to use basic authentication.
- Your Workday tenant ID, WSDL URL, and the Workday tenant timezone.

> **WORKDAY SETUP**
> 
> You must complete the Workday-side setup for your authentication method before you create the connection in Workato. Refer to the [Workday connector documentation](/en/connectors/workday#connection-setup) for the full ISU registration, security group, domain access, and API client setup procedures.

## Supported connection types

Workday pipelines support cloud and on-prem connections, with OAuth 2.0 or basic authentication.

### Connection type

Workato reaches your Workday tenant through one of the following routes:

- **Cloud**: Connect directly from Workato's cloud to your Workday tenant.
- **On-prem group**: Connect through an on-prem group when network or security policy requires it.

### Authentication type

The authentication type determines whether the pipeline can access custom objects and Workday Query Language (WQL) data, and how the connection authenticates against your tenant.

- **OAuth 2.0**: Authenticate through a registered API client for integrations in Workday using a non-expiring refresh token. OAuth 2.0 is required to work with custom objects and WQL.
- **Basic authentication**: Authenticate with the ISU login name and password. Custom objects and WQL aren't available with this type.

## Connect to Workday

Complete the following steps to connect Workday as a data pipeline source. Select the tab that matches the authentication type you plan to use.

Connect to Workday

**OAuth 2.0**

1. Select **Create > Connection** or press C twice.
   
2. Search for `Workday` and select it as your app.
   
3. Enter a name in the **Connection name** field.
   
   ![Configure your Workday connection](/assets/configure-workday-connection-oauth.CBpiqpm9.png)_Configure your Workday connection_
   
4. Use the **Location** drop-down menu to select the project where you plan to store the connection.
   
5. Use the **Connection type** drop-down menu to select **Cloud**.
   
6. Select **OAuth 2.0** in the **Authentication type** field. This method is required to work with custom objects and to query data using Workday Query Language (WQL) with the Workday REST API.
   
7. Enter your Workday tenant ID in the **Tenant ID** field. Your tenant ID is the value that appears in the URL when you log in to Workday. For example, in `https://impl.workday.com/sample_company/d/home.htmld`, the tenant ID is `sample_company`.
   
8. Enter your Workday WSDL URL in the **WSDL URL** field. For example, `https://wd2-impl-services1.workday.com/ccx/service/`.
   
9. Enter the client ID from your Workday API client settings in the **Client ID** field.
   
10. Enter the client secret from your Workday API client settings in the **Client secret** field.
    
11. Enter your non-expiring refresh token in the **Refresh token** field. Refer to [Generate a non-expiring refresh token](/en/connectors/workday#register-api-client) for steps.
    
12. Enter the authorization endpoint from your Workday API client settings in the **Authorization endpoint** field.
    
13. Enter the token endpoint from your Workday API client settings in the **Token endpoint** field.
    
14. Use the **Workday tenant timezone** drop-down menu to select the timezone configured in your Workday tenant. Workday returns data effective from the current day in PST by default. Selecting a timezone ensures retrieved data is consistent with your tenant.
    
15. Optional. Expand **Advanced settings** to configure the **Advanced XML payload for multiple ID values**.
    
    Workato wraps each value in fields with multiple values within its own container by default when constructing the XML from your input.
    
    For example:
    
    ```
    <languages><language>english</language></languages><languages><language>chinese</language></languages>
    ```
    
    Workato unwraps these values and presents them in a single container if you set the value to **Yes**:
    
    ```
    <languages><language>english</language><language>chinese</language></languages>
    ```
    
    Consider enabling this when you encounter invalid payload errors.
    
16. Use the **Workday web services version** drop-down menu to select the API version you plan to use. Defaults to `45.1`. Refer to [API version](/en/connectors/workday#api-version) for the supported version list and version support policy.
    
17. Select **Connect** to verify and save the connection.
    

**Basic authentication**

1. Select **Create > Connection** or press C twice.
   
2. Search for `Workday` and select it as your app.
   
3. Enter a name in the **Connection name** field.
   
   ![Configure your Workday connection](/assets/configure-workday-connection-basic.DZeY_AC0.png)_Configure your Workday connection_
   
4. Use the **Location** drop-down menu to select the project where you plan to store the connection.
   
5. Use the **Connection type** drop-down menu to select **Cloud**.
   
6. Use the **Authentication type** drop-down menu to select **Basic**.
   
7. Enter your Workday tenant ID in the **Tenant ID** field.
   
8. Enter your Workday WSDL URL in the **WSDL URL** field.
   
9. Enter the ISU login name in the **Login name** field.
   
10. Enter the ISU password in the **Password** field.
    
11. Use the **Workday tenant timezone** drop-down menu to select the timezone configured in your Workday tenant.
    
12. Optional. Expand **Advanced settings** to configure the **Advanced XML payload for multiple ID values**.
    
    Workato wraps each value in fields with multiple values within its own container by default when constructing the XML from your input.
    
    For example:
    
    ```
    <languages><language>english</language></languages><languages><language>chinese</language></languages>
    ```
    
    Workato unwraps these values and presents them in a single container if you set the value to **Yes**:
    
    ```
    <languages><language>english</language><language>chinese</language></languages>
    ```
    
    Consider enabling this setting if you encounter invalid payload errors.
    
13. Use the **Workday web services version** drop-down menu to select the API version you plan to use. Defaults to `45.1`.
    
14. Select **Connect** to verify and save the connection.
    

## Configure the pipeline

Complete the following steps to configure Workday as your data pipeline source:

1. Select **Create > Data pipeline** or press C+I.
   
2. Enter a name for the data pipeline in the **Data pipeline name** field.
   
   ![Data pipeline setup](/assets/set-up-pipeline.Cxx6hIk2.png)_Data pipeline setup_
   
3. Use the **Location** drop-down menu to select the project where you plan to store the data pipeline.
   
4. Click **Start building**.
   
5. Click the **Extract new/updated records from source app** trigger. This trigger defines how the pipeline retrieves data from Workday.
   
   ![Configure the Extract new/updated records from source app trigger](/assets/choose-source-app.B2OOUpgY.png)_Configure the Extract new/updated records from source app trigger_
   
6. Use the **Your Connected Source Apps** drop-down menu to select **Workday**.
   
7. Choose the Workday connection you plan to use for this pipeline. Alternatively, click **\+ New connection** to create a new connection.
   
8. Click **Add object** to open the **Add new objects** panel.
   
   ![Add objects](/assets/add-objects-workday.BAZPfRsR.png)_Add objects_
   
9. Search or browse the list of available Workday objects, select the objects you plan to sync, and click **Add**.
   
10. Review and customize the schema for each selected object. When you select an object, the pipeline automatically fetches its schema to ensure the destination matches the source.
    
    ![Review schema](/assets/review-schema-workday.BChWTXUu.png)_Review schema_
    
    Expand any object to view its fields. Keep all fields selected to extract all available data, or deselect specific fields to exclude them from data extraction and schema replication.
    
11. Optional. Configure field-level data protection by expanding an object and choosing how to handle each field:
    
    - **Replicate as is**: Data values at the source replicate identically to the destination.
    - **Hash**: Hash sensitive data values in the field before syncing to your destination.
    
    Workato recommends hashing personally identifiable information (PII) and other sensitive fields.
    
12. Click **Add object** again to add more objects. Repeat this step to include additional Workday objects in your pipeline.
    
13. Use the **Choose how to handle schema changes** drop-down menu to select a schema drift handling option:
    
    - **Auto-sync new fields**: Automatically detects and syncs new fields added in the source.
    - **Block new fields**: Keeps the schema fixed after the pipeline starts. You must add new fields manually. This option may cause the destination to fall out of sync if the source schema updates.
    
    Refer to [Schema replication and schema drift management](/en/data-orchestration/data-pipeline-recipe/concepts#schema-drift) for more information.
    
14. Choose either a standard time-based schedule or define a custom cron expression in the **Frequency** field. This determines how often the pipeline syncs data from Workday to the destination.
    
    **Time-based schedule**
    
    1. Select the **Time unit**, such as **Minutes**, **Hours**, or **Days**.
       
    2. Specify the sync interval in the **Trigger every** field.
       
       For example, the pipeline syncs every 6 hours if you select **Hours** as the **Time unit** and enter `6` in the **Trigger every** field.
       
       The minimum interval you can set is 15 minutes.
       
    3. Select a start date for the historical data sync in the **When first started, this pipeline should pick up records from** field. This defines the earliest date from which the pipeline extracts records. The pipeline picks up all available records from the source if you leave this field blank.
       
       You can't change this value after you run the pipeline.
       
    4. Click **Save** to save your progress before you [configure your data pipeline destination](/en/data-orchestration/data-pipeline-recipe/configure-pipeline-destinations#configure‒how‒data‒is‒loaded‒in‒the‒workato‒data‒pipeline).
       
    
    **Cron-based scheduling**
    
    1. Use the **Time unit** drop-down menu to select **Custom schedule**.
       
    2. Enter an expression in the **Cron expression** field using the format:
       
       ```text
       [minute] [hour] [day of month] [month] [day of week]
       ```
       
       The minimum interval for cron schedules is 15 minutes.
       
       For example, enter the following expression to sync every day at 8:00 AM UTC:
       
       ```text
       0 8 * * *
       ```
       
    3. Optional. Select a **Timezone** for the cron expression. Leave blank to use `Etc/UTC`.
       
    4. Select a start date for the historical data sync in the **When first started, this pipeline should pick up records from** field. This defines the earliest date from which the pipeline extracts records. The pipeline picks up all available records from the source if you leave this field blank.
       
       You can't change this value after you run the pipeline.
       
    5. Click **Save** to save your progress before you [configure your data pipeline destination](/en/data-orchestration/data-pipeline-recipe/configure-pipeline-destinations#configure‒how‒data‒is‒loaded‒in‒the‒workato‒data‒pipeline).
       
    
    The historical start date applies to objects that support an API-level filter.
    

## Supported Workday objects

Workday pipelines sync data from business objects exposed through the Workday Web Services API. Workato discovers the available objects when you select **Add object** during pipeline configuration. The picker reflects what's available for your Workday tenant. Additional objects may appear depending on your tenant configuration and authentication type, including custom objects and WQL-backed objects when you connect with OAuth 2.0.

The following objects are commonly available, grouped by functional area:

### Workforce

Worker, position, and job structure records.

| Object | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Workers` | Employee worker records. |
| `Contingent_Workers` | Non-employee worker records, such as contractors and temporary staff. |
| `Worker_Compensation` | Compensation assignments and history for workers. |
| `Positions` | Position records, including filled and unfilled positions. |
| `Job_Profiles` | Job profile definitions used to standardize roles. |
| `Job_Families` | Job family groupings used to classify related job profiles. |
| `Job_Categories` | Job category classifications. |

### Organization structure

Organizational units, legal entities, and locations.

| Object | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Organizations` | Organization records, such as supervisory and functional organizations. |
| `Locations` | Physical and logical location records. |
| `Workday_Companies` | Company entity records. |
| `Cost_Centers` | Cost center organization records. |

### Compensation and payroll

Pay structures, payroll inputs, and payroll results.

| Object | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Compensation_Plans` | Compensation plan definitions. |
| `Compensation_Grades` | Pay grade definitions and ranges. |
| `Payroll_Results` | Processed payroll output records. |
| `Payroll_Inputs` | Payroll input records submitted to a pay run. |
| `Offcycle_Payments` | One-time payment records processed outside the standard pay cycle. |
| `Currency_Conversion_Rates` | Currency conversion rate records. |

### Recruiting

Requisitions, candidates, and interview data.

| Object | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Job_Requisitions` | Open and historical job requisition records. |
| `Candidates` | Candidate records for talent sourcing. |
| `Applicants` | Applicant records for specific requisitions. |
| `Interview_Feedback` | Interview feedback submitted by interviewers. |

### Time and absence

Time entry, time off balances, and absence overrides.

| Object | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Time_Requests` | Time entry and time off request records. |
| `Calculated_Time_Blocks` | Calculated time block records derived from time entries. |
| `Time_Off_Plan_Balances` | Time off plan balance records for workers. |
| `Override_Balances` | Manual balance override records. |
| `Carryover_Overrides` | Manual carryover override records. |
| `Accrual_Expiration_Overrides` | Manual accrual expiration override records. |
| `Absence_Inputs` | Absence input records submitted to absence plans. |

### Talent and performance

Goals, competencies, reviews, and feedback.

| Object | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Organization_Goals` | Organization-level goal records. |
| `Goal_Units` | Goal unit definitions used to measure goals. |
| `Certifications` | Worker certification records. |
| `Competencies` | Competency definitions and worker competency records. |
| `Rating_Scales` | Rating scale definitions used in reviews and assessments. |
| `Review_Types` | Performance review type definitions. |
| `Feedback_Badges` | Feedback badge records awarded to workers. |

### Financials

General ledger, suppliers, projects, and payment data.

| Object | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Accounting_Journals` | Accounting journal entry records. |
| `Suppliers` | Supplier records. |
| `Ledger_Accounts` | General ledger account records. |
| `Revenue_Categories` | Revenue category records. |
| `Payment_Messages` | Payment message records. |
| `Projects` | Project records. |

## Sync modes

Workday data pipelines support full refresh and incremental sync.

### Full refresh

A full refresh sync reads all available records for the object from Workday on every pipeline run. Use full refresh for objects when you need a complete snapshot of the data on each sync.

Objects with a primary key merge into the existing destination table, so records deleted in Workday stay in the table. Objects without a primary key overwrite the destination table on every run.

### Incremental sync

An incremental sync fetches only records that are new or changed since the last successful sync run.

## Schema and data type handling

Workday pipelines deliver standard business object data as a JSON document rather than flattening the underlying structure into individual columns. Parse the JSON column in your destination to work with specific Workday fields downstream. The JSON field is included by default. You can deselect the JSON field to remove the record content from sync, leaving only the identifier and metadata fields.

Each standard object also includes a primary key for the Workday record identifier, an optional descriptor field, and a `Workato Is Deleted` flag that you can use to identify deleted records.

## Workday limitations

The following limitations apply when you use Workday as a data pipeline source:

### Minimum sync frequency

The minimum supported sync interval is 15 minutes.

### Authentication type affects object availability

Custom objects and WQL-backed objects require OAuth 2.0 authentication. These objects aren't available when you connect with basic authentication.

### API version support

Workato supports a limited set of Workday Web Services API versions. Connections using removed versions are automatically upgraded to the earliest available version. Refer to [Version support policy](/en/connectors/workday#api-version) for more information.
